articles.title: Three to tango: On Trump, Xi, Putin trilateral summit
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: U.S., China, Russia must draw up a roadmap for talks on nuclear weapons

The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

Editorial Context: Three to tango: On Trump, Xi, Putin trilateral summit. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

articles.title: Going public on AI: On Anthropic IPO
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India can no longer afford its silence on the multi-trillion dollar AI arms race

The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Anthropic , PBC is a mile marker in the arms race to develop superintelligent systems driven by generative AI . Traders valued the firm at $1.27 trillion, a denomination that is bound to become more and more familiar in an industry backed by an endless appetite for capital and unprecedented forms of financialisation. Anthropic’s statements emphasise warnings on the safety of its systems and the consequences of unbridled development of advanced systems. In the history of the development of this technology, this PR spin may just be a blip. After all, their testing has led to AI agents that have broken out of sandboxes and infected unsuspecting organisations’ internal systems: a deluge of agentic chaos that is already a reality has led to little signs of the firm backing its words with action. A familiar trend is playing out, with open source LLMs showing frontier capabilities that can back their erratic impulses, appearing in the space of just months, or sometimes weeks. Advocates of pacing the frontier and managing these emerging risks have been marginalised in a way that has little precedent in this century. It is time for governments to get involved, and specifically, for India to raise its voice on these risks, loudly and unequivocally.

While India’s AI industry is nascent, its positions on international forums carry the weight of a sixth of humanity. A mix of cynical calculations and practical considerations have blunted the use of that voice, for example in the U.S.’s hugely destabilising war of choice against Iran, and Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. In taking a strong position on what could be the defining transformation of this decade, India has little to lose, and a lot to contribute. India’s AI policies are geared towards diffusion and research of helpful capabilities that can trickle down to the common citizen. The capabilities that the Union government and State governments seek to boost by leveraging AI are removed from the frontier research wreaking havoc within the information security profession around the world. Out-of-control AI agents promise, moreover, significant disruption to outdated government and private systems online. While India has little commercial leverage to curb San Francisco’s accelerationism, its voice is sure to be noticed. India’s focus on AI in international fora, such as the AI Impact Summit in Delhi, has been on consensus. This approach must change. India cannot be silent amid a U.S.-China technological race which could lead to catastrophic damage. New Delhi must not allow the U.S. to stop it from pushing for AI safety.
Editorial Context: Going public on AI: On Anthropic IPO. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

articles.summary: India can no longer afford its silence on the multi-trillion dollar AI arms race
articles.keyPoints:
• India can no longer afford its silence on the multi-trillion dollar AI arms race
• The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Anthropic , PBC is a mile marker in the arms race to develop superintelligent systems driven by generative AI . Traders valued the firm at $1.27 trillion, a denomination that is bound to become more and more familiar in an industry backed by an endless appetite for capital and unprecedented forms of financialisation. Anthropic’s statements emphasise warnings on the safety of its systems and the consequences of unbridled development of advanced systems. In the history of the development of this technology, this PR spin may just be a blip. After all, their testing has led to AI agents that have broken out of sandboxes and infected unsuspecting organisations’ internal systems: a deluge of agentic chaos that is already a reality has led to little signs of the firm backing its words with action. A familiar trend is playing out, with open source LLMs showing frontier capabilities that can back their erratic impulses, appearing in the space of just months, or sometimes weeks. Advocates of pacing the frontier and managing these emerging risks have been marginalised in a way that has little precedent in this century. It is time for governments to get involved, and specifically, for India to raise its voice on these risks, loudly and unequivocally.
• While India’s AI industry is nascent, its positions on international forums carry the weight of a sixth of humanity. A mix of cynical calculations and practical considerations have blunted the use of that voice, for example in the U.S.’s hugely destabilising war of choice against Iran, and Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. In taking a strong position on what could be the defining transformation of this decade, India has little to lose, and a lot to contribute. India’s AI policies are geared towards diffusion and research of helpful capabilities that can trickle down to the common citizen. The capabilities that the Union government and State governments seek to boost by leveraging AI are removed from the frontier research wreaking havoc within the information security profession around the world. Out-of-control AI agents promise, moreover, significant disruption to outdated government and private systems online. While India has little commercial leverage to curb San Francisco’s accelerationism, its voice is sure to be noticed. India’s focus on AI in international fora, such as the AI Impact Summit in Delhi, has been on consensus. This approach must change. India cannot be silent amid a U.S.-China technological race which could lead to catastrophic damage. New Delhi must not allow the U.S. to stop it from pushing for AI safety.

fullParagraphs: The ECI offers relief to a section of deleted electors but SIR’s flaws remain

Following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in some States that had undergone the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) , mostly in Phases 1 and 2, some 74 lakh names were added onto the electoral rolls. This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Draft deletions in Phase 3 of the SIR averaged 17% , and reached 32.8% in Delhi . The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number.

These “corrective” measures follow the Supreme Court’s observation on October 28 that forcing deleted electors to re-enrol through Form 6, meant for new voters, was an “error”. The ECI’s use of remedies that existed in the registration rules is a tacit admission that it went wrong during the SIR. But the measures are limited. They reach roughly 4.5 crore of the 13.37 crore struck off the draft rolls and do not cover electors who moved out of their States. Electors in States where the SIR has concluded, including Bihar and West Bengal, which have already voted on the SIR rolls, can return only through the SSR, by filing Form 6 as new voters, with fresh EPIC numbers and no record that they were ever on the roll. In essence, the structure of the SIR remains intact. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.

articles.title: Talks without peace: On Russia, Ukraine, U.S. talks
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Europe must be part of any settlement on the Ukraine war

The trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. earlier this month failed to produce a major breakthrough or bridge the wide gap between Kyiv and Moscow. Yet, they were a good beginning towards finding a political settlement to Europe’s longest war since the Second World War . In the two-day talks, hosted by the U.S., the warring sides agreed on some humanitarian measures, including prisoner exchange. U.S. representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow after the talks to discuss the proposal. In the next stage, U.S., Ukrainian and European officials will meet in Berlin to discuss a coordinated European and Ukrainian position towards the peace process. As of now, Russian and Ukrainian positions remain far apart. Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the territories of Donbas it still controls to stop attacks. Russia also wants to introduce limits to Ukrainian military capabilities and Kyiv to declare neutrality (give up its NATO ambitions). Ukraine, on the other hand, has rejected making any territorial concessions for a settlement and asked for security guarantees from the West so that Russia would not attack the country again.

That Ukraine survived Russia’s invasion and continued to resist Russian forces for almost five years is no small feat. But it has also paid a huge price for its resistance. The country has lost more than 20% of its territory. Millions have fled, while men of fighting age are being drafted into the military . Ukraine’s economy is kept afloat by European support, while its military continues to rely on NATO for weapons and other supplies. Until recently, the West stood united in its support for Ukraine against Russia, but that unity has since begun to fray. U.S. President Donald Trump, who has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, is seeking to reset Washington’s ties with Moscow . European leaders, who initially sought to isolate Russia, have also started reestablishing contacts with the Kremlin. In October, Finnish and Norwegian leaders held direct talks with Mr. Putin. To be sure, Ukraine’s long-range strikes can hurt Russia, as the recent attack on the Kerch Bridge demonstrated. But such strikes are unlikely to change the Kremlin’s thinking about the war. As the conflict drags on, Ukraine’s position is weakening, and its allies are growing increasingly divided. After almost five years, Russia has failed to take a decisive victory. Ukraine does not have a credible path towards victory either. A diplomatic settlement, therefore, is the only way forward. The Abu Dhabi talks recognised this reality. But for the process to be meaningful, Europe must also be brought to the negotiating table.

articles.summary: Europe must be part of any settlement on the Ukraine war
articles.keyPoints:
• Europe must be part of any settlement on the Ukraine war
• The trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. earlier this month failed to produce a major breakthrough or bridge the wide gap between Kyiv and Moscow. Yet, they were a good beginning towards finding a political settlement to Europe’s longest war since the Second World War . In the two-day talks, hosted by the U.S., the warring sides agreed on some humanitarian measures, including prisoner exchange. U.S. representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow after the talks to discuss the proposal. In the next stage, U.S., Ukrainian and European officials will meet in Berlin to discuss a coordinated European and Ukrainian position towards the peace process. As of now, Russian and Ukrainian positions remain far apart. Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the territories of Donbas it still controls to stop attacks. Russia also wants to introduce limits to Ukrainian military capabilities and Kyiv to declare neutrality (give up its NATO ambitions). Ukraine, on the other hand, has rejected making any territorial concessions for a settlement and asked for security guarantees from the West so that Russia would not attack the country again.
• That Ukraine survived Russia’s invasion and continued to resist Russian forces for almost five years is no small feat. But it has also paid a huge price for its resistance. The country has lost more than 20% of its territory. Millions have fled, while men of fighting age are being drafted into the military . Ukraine’s economy is kept afloat by European support, while its military continues to rely on NATO for weapons and other supplies. Until recently, the West stood united in its support for Ukraine against Russia, but that unity has since begun to fray. U.S. President Donald Trump, who has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, is seeking to reset Washington’s ties with Moscow . European leaders, who initially sought to isolate Russia, have also started reestablishing contacts with the Kremlin. In October, Finnish and Norwegian leaders held direct talks with Mr. Putin. To be sure, Ukraine’s long-range strikes can hurt Russia, as the recent attack on the Kerch Bridge demonstrated. But such strikes are unlikely to change the Kremlin’s thinking about the war. As the conflict drags on, Ukraine’s position is weakening, and its allies are growing increasingly divided. After almost five years, Russia has failed to take a decisive victory. Ukraine does not have a credible path towards victory either. A diplomatic settlement, therefore, is the only way forward. The Abu Dhabi talks recognised this reality. But for the process to be meaningful, Europe must also be brought to the negotiating table.

fullParagraphs: India needs to be at its best in Tests against New Zealand

New Zealand at home remains an indomitable cricketing opposition. Even the great West Indian squad led by Clive Lloyd suffered a 0-1 Test series defeat in 1980. Pitches that look lush as English meadows, the wind that is often bone-chilling cold, and fast bowlers relishing their prospects, make any tour of New Zealand a difficult outing. So far, the visiting Indians have done well, having won the T20I and ODI series, but the real contest starts with the first Test at Wellington’s Basin Reserve from Thursday. The Shubman Gill-led men’s last overseas tour of Sri Lanka ended with a middling 1-0 victory in the two Tests, but more needs to be done against New Zealand in the latest two-Test series. Placed fourth in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) table, and with hopes of securing a final berth seemingly fragile, India is in a win-all-games situation first up against New Zealand and later when Australia arrives next year. Against current WTC topper New Zealand, the Indian batters have to stay anchored. This is a line-up that no longer has Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Cheteshwar Pujara and Ajinkya Rahane. Gill and company get another opportunity to reiterate their credentials.

For some rugged inspiration they need not look beyond coach Gautam Gambhir in their dressing room. The doughty former India opener batted for 643 minutes while scoring a match-saving 137 in the Napier Test during the 2009 tour. The southpaw will be hoping that the current batting unit, which is high on flair, will remain sober and effectively counter the host. K.L. Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal and Gill have the onerous task of negating the New Zealand seamers in their backyard. Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel add depth, and if the former can successfully unleash his maverick batting approach, India can upset the host’s best-laid plans. New Zealand will miss the retired Kane Williamson but its batters would be comfortable on familiar surfaces. For India, much would hinge on how Jasprit Bumrah bowls. If the spearhead clicks, then it becomes easier for much of his support-cast that includes the persevering Mohammed Siraj, who was a touch rusty in Sri Lanka. From the squads of the past to the present unit, Ravindra Jadeja remains the link. Whether he will get a role to play or whether the management prefers an all-pace attack, remains a matter of conjecture. The home team led by Tom Latham will depend on Matt Henry, Kyle Jameson and other pacers, to choke the Indian batters. A hard task awaits India, first at Wellington and then at Christchurch.

articles.title: Many imperatives: On India’s Asia diplomacy
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India must shore up its partnerships in the Asian region

Each year, the summits of the 11-member Association of South-East Asian Nations mark an important moment on the diplomatic calendar: India is able to interact with all of its partners in the Indo-Pacific and engage global powers at the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s talks with Indo-Pacific players focused on a future shaped “not by competition, but by cooperation”. This year, the summit in Manila hosted by the Philippines had many other imperatives. These were the first ASEAN summits since the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran and Iran’s Hormuz blockade and strikes on Gulf countries that have upended energy and trade across South and South East Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world during the EAS was aimed as much at leaders from the U.S., Russia and China as it was for the region. The visit had a bilateral context — the Philippines and India have intensified ties considerably in the past year, since the visit of President Bongbong Marcos to Delhi in August 2025, including the upgradation of the Strategic Partnership, maritime exchanges and negotiations over the supply of more Indian-made Brahmos missile battery systems to the Philippines. This year, after months of concerns about U.S. President Donald Trump’s lack of interest in the Quad grouping, the U.S. decided to host a summit of U.S.-India-Australia-Japan Quad leaders on the side-lines of the ASEAN summits, the first time the summit has been held in a non-Quad country.

Given the stakes, there were several outcomes from all the three summits that PM Modi attended back-to-back on Tuesday — the ASEAN India Summit launched a new cooperation on disaster management, and the East Asia Summit focused on countering cyber-crime. PM Modi’s announcement that India would give all ASEAN citizens free tourist visas is expected to increase people-to-people interactions and trade. At the Quad summit, President Trump made a number of announcements including the launch of a Quad Business leaders forum, to be held in Mumbai next year, and the first Quad naval exercises with patrol aircraft. However, the outcomes in Manila paled in significance to the anticipation over Mr. Trump’s next stop in Shenzhen for the Asia Pacific Economic Conference (APEC), with an unprecedented three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping planned on Thursday. New Delhi must watch the outcomes of that summit among the “global superpowers” much more closely.

articles.title: In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare. Poverty, land alienation, and the erosion of traditional food systems, are taking a toll on maternal and child health in this predominantly tribal region of Keralam

Between the pages of a logbook recording Dakshina’s treatment are ₹100, ₹50, ₹20, and ₹10 notes. Dakshina’s mother, Minnal Rani, had filed them away for her daughter’s medical expenses. The child is gone, but the money remains untouched. “We will never spend it,” she says, fighting back tears.

Dakshina was five months old when doctors detected a hole in her heart. Born on June 13, 2025, she was taken to many hospitals, including one in Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam’s capital. With surgery ruled out, she was eventually referred to a cooperative hospital at Perinthalmanna, in Malappuram district, a two-and-a-half-hour drive away from home. She died here, on April 13, 2026.
Rani and her husband Chandra Sekhar say the hospital refused to release their daughter’s body until they paid a bill of ₹10,000. They managed to raise the money with the help of a ward councillor.
“We buried her under that tree,” says Rani, pointing to a coconut tree near their house at Vechapathi hamlet in Sholayur panchayat of Attappadi, Palakkad district.

Dakshina’s death is among a series of 10 infant deaths reported this year from Attappadi, a predominantly tribal settlement. There have been four back-to-back deaths in October. Of the 10 infant deaths, six involved congenital anomalies, with heart defects among the commonly reported conditions. An expert committee of doctors and researchers is examining the deaths.
Ground Zero / Keralam / infants / health / government health care

articles.title: Digital planetariums, education centres will be established in all divisions: Bihar Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Requisition for appointment of 1,061 faculty posts for Engineering Colleges and 354 faculty posts for polytechnic colleges sent to BPSC

With a view to developing a scientific temperament among students and the general public, state-of-the-art “digital planetariums and education centres” will be established in all the divisions of the state, Bihar Science and Technology Minister Sheela Kumari said on Friday (November 20, 2026).
“The district magistrates of the districts concerned have been requested to provide a minimum of two acres of land for the purpose,” Ms. Kumari said while addressing a press conference in Patna.

These centres will provide children and young people with practical knowledge of astronomy and space research, she said, while praising Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary’s leadership for the initiative.
In reply to a query, she said that these planetariums will be ready in a year.

The Minister further stated that digital planetariums/space and astronomy education centres will also be established in three districts—East Champaran, Jamui, and Purnea—as part of the Union Ministry of Culture’s Scheme for Promotion of Culture and Science (SPOCS).

“The total estimated project cost is ₹39.00 crore, which will be funded with central assistance,” she said, adding that the target is to commence construction work during the current financial year, 2026-27.

A digital planetarium uses computer software and high-resolution digital projectors (or LED panels) to display 3D simulations of the night sky, space travel, and science visuals inside a dome theatre. Unlike traditional optical-mechanical projectors that only show fixed star positions, digital systems can fly viewers through galaxies, simulate different time periods, and play full-dome films.
Ms. Kumari was accompanied by Department Secretary Himanshu Sharma and a host of other senior officials during the press conference.

In order to generate public interest in science and technology, efforts are also being made to operate mobile science exhibition buses, observatory domes, and astro parks through the National Council of Science Museums.

Notably, the state currently has two functional planetariums—one each in Patna and Darbhanga. The planetarium in Darbhanga was established in 2023, while the renovation of the Patna planetarium has already been completed.

articles.title: Transgender persons to be roped in for tax collection in West Bengal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: West Bengal Minister Agnimitra Paul launches a programme to provide dignified, alternative livelihoods to trans persons

The West Bengal government will engage transgender persons to collect municipal tax and spread traffic awareness. Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Minister Agnimitra Paul said the initiative, called “Brihannala Brigade”, will provide an opportunity for a dignified livelihood for the transpersons.

“The CM wishes that they (transgender people no) longer have to resort to begging at traffic signals; instead, we want to offer them an alternative, respectable livelihood. We have decided that those among them who are interested will receive training from the police and be deployed at traffic signals. Their role will be to sensitise the public about traffic rules and safety measures,” Ms. Paul said on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

She further added that another group of transgender persons would be trained to collect outstanding taxes, which could help address the staff shortage that leads to delayed collections and large pending amounts.

The Minister also added that each of these transgender individuals will be provided with training to engage in this work so that they can conduct better public interaction and do their work seamlessly. They will receive a stipend for the work, Ms. Paul said.

The West Bengal government has started an initiative to offer relief in paying outstanding property taxes, including in the actual sums and interest, to encourage defaulters to pay their outstanding balances.
According to Kolkata Municipal Corporation estimates, they have around ₹6800 crore outstanding property tax pending, including personal properties, mixed-use properties, and commercial properties.

In 2022, the previous Mamata Banerjee government decided to allow transgender persons to apply for government jobs under the general category to help them have better opportunities in employment. A Transgender Development Board was set up in 2017, but the board could not undertake many activities for the welfare of members of the community. The last census carried out in the state in 2011 put the number of transgender people in the state at 30,349. The actual number of people of the third gender may be higher, several groups working for the community say.

articles.title: Trinamool supporters attacked outside the police station as police questioned Abhishek
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The supporters of Trinamool had gathered outside the police station in support of Abhishek Banerjee

Supporters of Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) were allegedly attacked on Friday (November 20, 2026) by supporters of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) outside a police station while party leader Abhishek Banerjee was being questioned by Kolkata Police at the Girish Park police station.

Videos of the scuffle and the assault on women supporters of the Trinamool were shared on social media and by the Mamata AITC. In the videos, groups of women alleged to be BJP supporters were seen chasing another group of women. Supporters of the Trinamool had gathered outside the police station in support of Abhishek Banerjee. articles.title: Chandel district official issues advisory after spurious liquor kills 11 in Manipur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Chandel district authorities have urged the people to report suspected manufacturing, storage, sale or distribution of adulterated liquor
Manipur’s Chandel district administration on Friday (November 20, 2026) issued an advisory, urging people to report suspected manufacturing, storage, sale or distribution of adulterated liquor.
The public advisory followed the death of 11 people due to consumption of spurious liquor in the district’s Chakpikarong Sub-Division. The deaths have been reported since Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

According to a statement from the Chief Minister’s Office, 180 others are undergoing treatment at two private hospitals in Imphal. Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited these hospitals on Friday and took stock of the treatment being provided to the patients.

Advising the general public to exercise utmost caution, the district administration said the cause of the deaths was yet to be “medically and scientifically established”. It asked people to refrain from consuming locally brewed liquor or alcoholic beverages of doubtful origin, particularly from suspected sources in the affected areas.

“Any person experiencing vomiting, abdominal pain, headache, dizziness, blurred vision, breathing difficulty or other unusual symptoms following alcohol consumption should immediately seek medical attention at the nearest facility,” the advisory read.
It also advised people who may have consumed liquor from the same suspected source to seek medical evaluation even if they are not experiencing symptoms.

“The public is requested to report suspected manufacturing, storage, sale or distribution of adulterated liquor to the nearest police station or the concerned authorities,” the advisory further read, requesting village authorities, civil society organisations, women’s organisations and youth clubs to assist in spreading awareness.

The Manipur government partially lifted 30 years of alcohol prohibition in December 2023, although extremist groups in the State continue to target liquor businesses. Years of prohibition led to certain areas turning into local liquor dens, selling alcoholic beverages of suspect quality.
Spurious liquor has claimed lives in other northeastern States where prohibition is enforced. For instance, 23 people were killed in Nagaland’s Mokokchung and Tuensang districts about two months ago.

articles.title: Coal auction rounds attract 85 bids; 20 first-time players enter sector
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The 16th round of commercial mine auctions put forth 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.
The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions has attracted 83 bids for 17 coal blocks with 20 first-time bidders seeking to enter commercial coal mining, signalling fresh interest in the sector.
The Union Coal Ministry said on Friday that 17 blocks offered in the latest round received 83 bids. In addition, the second attempt to auction one coal block from the 15th round attracted two bids.
Taking the 26 blocks covered by the auction process into account, the number of bids has quadrupled compared with the previous round, the ministry said.
The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions was launched on September 17, offering 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.

“Competition in the current round has been intense, with 16 of the 26 blocks attracting multiple bids. The round has also brought 20 first-time bidders into the commercial coal mining regime, a clear sign that the sector continues to draw new capital and new players,” the ministry said in a statement.

Since the introduction of the commercial coal mining auction regime in June 2020, the government has auctioned 145 coal mines across 15 rounds. These mines are estimated to generate annual revenues of around ₹47,500 crore, according to government estimates.

articles.title: CEA flags need to align capital markets with India’s development priorities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Equity market capitalisation stood at around 130% of GDP, while the corporate bond market accounted for only about 16%.

Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran has called for a greater role for Indian capital markets in channelising household savings into productive investments, stressing the importance of patient capital in meeting the country’s long-term development needs.

Speaking at the CII Financial Summit in Mumbai, Mr. Nageswaran said sectors such as infrastructure, manufacturing, agriculture and mineral exploration required long-term financing, given their extended investment horizons.
Highlighting the imbalance in India’s financial markets, he pointed out that equity market capitalisation stood at around 130% of GDP, while the corporate bond market accounted for only about 16%.

While acknowledging that technology had improved market access, settlement systems and transaction security, he said these advances had not necessarily translated into better outcomes for investors or the real economy.

“A safer machine is not the same as a better outcome,” he said, emphasising that technological innovation should ultimately strengthen the capital market’s core function of converting savings into productive investments.
Cautioning against a consumption-led economic model, Mr. Nageswaran said, “An economy that is consumption-oriented may not be the most suited one for India’s development context.”

Echoing the need to promote long-term savings, Gaurav Mathur, founder and managing director of SafeGold, called for tax incentives to encourage investors to hold financial assets for longer periods. He stressed that savings policies should reflect individuals’ financial circumstances and different stages of life.

“It’s a matter of constructive partnership between regulators and financial intermediaries, where you incentivise long-term saving behaviour at the appropriate stages in life,” Mr. Mathur said, adding that incentives should particularly target wealthier individuals with greater capacity to save.

Meanwhile, Nilesh Shah, managing director of Kotak Mahindra Asset Management Company and part-time member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, underscored the need to strengthen financial literacy and encourage voluntary pension savings. He said these measures were increasingly important amid uncertainties over employment and income in a technology-driven economy.

articles.title: How AI could reshape global growth and productivity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: A key expected impact of AI is an unprecedented rise in labour productivity, as its success as a technological revolution is premised on such an increase; what remains to be seen is how pervasive its impact will be across different sectors of the economy

Many have likened the artificial intelligence (AI) phenomenon to the inventions of the steam engine or internal combustion engine in the 18th and 19th centuries, respectively. Only time can tell whether AI is epochal of that kind. In this two-part piece, we discuss the possible impact it may have on the global economy as a whole.

A key impact of AI is considered to be an unprecedented rise in labour productivity. In fact, if there is one purpose AI is supposed to serve, it is enhancing labour productivity multifold. Since labour productivity is a key variable in this puzzle, consider what it constitutes of (Box 1) . It is a ratio of output and workers employed. Now this ratio can rise in three different ways — a rise in output for a given number of workers employed (rise in the numerator); a loss of jobs which leads to a fall in the denominator; more jobs are created, but the output rises faster than the jobs (while both the numerator and the denominator are rising, the numerator rises faster than the denominator).

There is usually a distinction drawn between a case where there is a net loss of jobs versus one where jobs grow, but the output grows even faster. The latter is preferred over the former. Even though AI may displace white-collar workers, it may generate more jobs for the blue-collar workers, so in the net there may not be a job loss with AI adoption across the economy. However, for the argument we make below, it does not matter which of the three sources leads to a rise in productivity. Why should the rise in labour productivity matter? There are two contrasting takes on this question in the economics discipline.

One which argues that productivity growth increases the growth of output in the economy. The idea is simple. Growth of output is a function of its two inputs — labour and capital. Since capital enhances the productivity of labour, the rate at which output can grow is the sum of the growth of the labour force and its productivity. So, if the workforce grows at 2% and productivity at 4%, the economy would stabilise at 6% growth over time. And if the rate of labour productivity rises, according to this framework, growth in the economy rises pari passu (Graph 1a).

Between the three variables — output growth, labour growth and productivity growth — output growth adjusts to the other two. This is what Robert Solow, a celebrated economist and a Nobel laureate, showed in a seminal paper on growth theory. What he did not explain though was why and where did this labour productivity rise come from. Much later, his successors argued that the growth of labour productivity depends on investment in human capital, research and development, patent regimes, etc., what came to be known as endogenous growth theories.

articles.title: OMCs achieve 0.08% biodiesel blending in H1, lower than target; cite feedstock shortage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: In the fiscal year 2025-26, OMCs had achieved an overall biodiesel blending of 0.18%

India’s three state-owned oil marketing companies (OMCs) – Indian Oil Corporation, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation and Bharat Petroleum Corporation – achieved an overall biodiesel blending of just 0.08% in the first half of FY27, “significantly below” the indicative target of 5% by 2030, citing limited feedstock availability.
Biodiesel is produced from various feedstocks, including non-edible vegetable oils, animal fat and recycled cooking oil.

Between April and September 2026, the three OMCs sold approximately 4,900 crore litres of diesel. Of this, more than 4,700 crore litres were sold without any biodiesel blending. The remaining 200 crore litres comprised diesel blended with approximately four crore litres of biodiesel, translating into an average blending rate of 2% in the blended portion, they said in a joint statement.
Consequently, biodiesel accounted for 0.08% of the total diesel sold by the OMCs during the six-month period.
The performance also marks a decline from FY26, when the three companies achieved an overall biodiesel blending rate of 0.18%.

The OMCs reiterated that biodiesel-blended diesel conforms to Bureau of Indian Standards specification BIS 1460, which prescribes requirements for automotive diesel fuel, and is covered under the publicly notified National Policy on Biofuels.

They also pointed out that biodiesel blending is an established global practice, with countries such as Indonesia, Malaysia and Brazil adopting blending levels ranging from 10% to 50%, depending on feedstock availability.

articles.title: Anthropic researcher says Claude solved maths’ greatest riddle
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics

A mathematician at AI company Anthropic said Friday (November 20, 2026) that he had used the firm’s Claude chatbot to prove the Riemann Hypothesis, a problem that has eluded mathematicians for more than 160 years.
“I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Levent Alpoge wrote in a four-page note released Friday (November 20, 2026).
The claim has not been independently verified, and the proof has not yet been reviewed by outside experts.

First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics.
It is one of seven Millennium Prize Problems selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute in 2000, which offers $1 million for a solution to each.
Under the institute’s rules, a solution must be published in a peer-reviewed journal and withstand two years of scrutiny.
Mr. Alpoge said the method also resolves a broader version of the problem known as the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis.

He said he and Claude had produced a version of the proof in Lean, a programming language that allows mathematical arguments to be checked by a computer, and that he was releasing only that version for now.
A full written argument would be extremely long, he said, adding that he had not yet mastered all of the mathematics involved and planned to write it up properly.

Mr. Alpoge said he had consulted Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei before announcing the result and acknowledged that its timing could be viewed cynically, without elaborating, though he was probably referring to this week’s record IPO.

articles.title: Estonia to close border with Russia, Moscow decries 'new Iron Curtain'
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: NATO and EU member ‌Estonia on November 15 accused Russian security services of staging an attempted ‌arson ⁠attack on an Estonian defence company, in what it said ⁠was the second such incident this year

Estonia will close its road border crossings with Russia on security grounds for at least six months, the Baltic country's government ‌said on Friday (November 20, 2026), prompting a warning from Moscow that it would respond with political and diplomatic measures.

NATO and EU member ‌Estonia on Sunday (November 15, 2026) accused Russian security services of staging an attempted ‌arson ⁠attack on an Estonian defence company, in what it said ⁠was the second such incident this year.
This would help address the wider security situation and limit Russia's ability to ​organise further attacks, Estonian Interior Minister ‌Igor Taro told a press conference.
"Russian security services are intimidating and trying to recruit our citizens who are travelling through our border checkpoints. This is something we cannot tolerate anymore," Mr. Taro said.
The Kremlin has ‌denied any involvement in the weekend arson attack.
Foreign Ministry spokeswoman ​Maria Zakharova on Friday (November 20, 2026) said that Russia would respond with political and diplomatic measures if Estonia went ahead with the ⁠closure.
"Such moves are tantamount to attempts to erect a new Iron Curtain under the false pretence of some sort of threat from the East," ‌Ms. Zakharova said.
Estonia, a strong supporter of Ukraine, currently has five crossing points where travellers can enter or leave Russia, according to the government.
Estonia's northern neighbour Finland shut its Russia border crossings in 2023, and has kept them closed since then, while southern Baltic nations Latvia and Lithuania maintain open crossings.

Thousands of people living in Estonia have family in ‌Russia or vice versa, as legacies of the Soviet era. The crossing at Narva, a ​majority Russian-speaking city on the Estonian side of the border, is also used by people travelling from further afield in ⁠Europe to reach St. Petersburg a few hours' drive away.

articles.title: Pakistan Army chief Munir vows to eliminate terrorism from country
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Pakistan overall witnessed a significant decline in terrorism-related violence during October, with attacks falling by 37%, deaths resulting from these attacks declining by 57%, and injuries decreasing by 71% compared to September, said Dawn newspaper report

Pakistan’s Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir on Friday (November 20, 2026) expressed the “unwavering resolve” of the security forces to eliminate terrorism from the country during a visit to the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.
Mr. Munir, who is also the Chief of Defence Forces (CDF), said this during a visit to Miranshah in North Waziristan district, the military's media wing said in a statement.

“He reaffirmed the unwavering resolve of the security forces, in close coordination with law enforcement agencies, to decisively eliminate the menace of terrorism and preserve the hard-earned peace and stability of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa,” the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement.
Mr. Munir also appreciated the KP police and expressed pride in its resilience and sacrifices against terrorism and Fitna-al-Khawarij.
The term Fitna-al-Khawarij is used by the federal government for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

During the visit, the CDF was given a comprehensive briefing on “the prevailing security situation, ongoing intelligence-based operations [IBO] and measures being undertaken to consolidate the gains achieved through sustained counter-terrorism efforts, “ the ISPR statement said.

The term Fitna-al-Khawarij is used by the federal government for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

articles.title: U.S. sanctions Myanmar armed group leader over scam links
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Treasury Department said on November 19 it had imposed an asset freeze on General Saw Shwe Wah, commander-in-chief of the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA), and one of his top officers, and had banned Americans from dealing with them
The United States has frozen the assets of the leader of an ethnic armed group in Myanmar and one of his lieutenants, accusing them of facilitating cyberscammers who target Americans.

Organised criminal gangs have, for years, carried out fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes from compounds in Southeast Asian nations, defrauding victims around the world of tens of billions of dollars annually.
The industry is adapting its operations in the wake of much-publicised crackdowns in Myanmar and Cambodia following Chinese pressure, often dissipating into smaller facilities in new locations.

The U.S. Treasury Department said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) it had imposed an asset freeze on General Saw Shwe Wah, commander-in-chief of the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA), and one of his top officers, and had banned Americans from dealing with them.
The DKBA is one of the myriad armed groups operating in Myanmar's borderlands, some of which have been fighting the government for decades.
It has signed a ceasefire with Yangon and is accused by the United States, which earlier sanctioned the organisation, of supporting scam centres.

"DKBA actors not only provide security for scam compounds and permit their continued operation, but also actively participate in violence against victims of human trafficking trapped inside the compounds," the U.S. Treasury said.
The DKBA's Colonel Saw A One, responsible for security in the Three Pagodas Pass area in Karen State near the Thai border, was also designated by the U.S. on Thursday (November 19, 2026).
Jason Tower, senior expert at the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime, told that last week the Three Pagodas Pass region has been a "major expansion area" for scam compounds.
The latest U.S. Treasury measures also sanctioned Zhao Hui, a China-born, naturalised Cambodian accused of running cyberscam compounds in Cambodia, and two of his companies.

articles.title: FDA sets up council for post-market review of vaccines, gene therapies
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The FDA said the council is intended to improve accountability and transparency as biologic products grow increasingly complex, particularly in cell and gene therapy, a sector that has seen rapid regulatory expansion in recent years

The US Food and Drug Administration said on Thursday it had established a new internal safety body within its biologics center, formalizing independent oversight of approved products such as vaccines, gene therapies and blood products once they reach the market.

The CBER Safety Council will report directly to the director of the FDA’s Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, structurally separating post-market safety reviews from the offices responsible for approving those products, the agency said.

The council supersedes CBER’s existing Safety Working Group, bringing together senior scientific and regulatory officials to review safety signals, conduct benefit-risk assessments and recommend regulatory actions as warranted.

The new structure formalizes an independent post-market review process at a time when regulators face mounting pressure to closely monitor newer biologic products, including gene and cell therapies, after approval, when they are used across far broader patient populations.
Its mandate will cover emerging safety concerns, potential labeling changes, risk-management measures and safety-related post-market studies, as well as advising on potential market withdrawals.

The FDA said the council is intended to improve accountability and transparency as biologic products grow increasingly complex, particularly in cell and gene therapy, a sector that has seen rapid regulatory expansion in recent years.

The council will coordinate with external bodies including the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the National Institutes of Health, drawing on surveillance systems such as the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) and the FDA Sentinel program.
The council takes effect on November 19; the agency said additional details on its structure and membership will be released later.

articles.title: Tiger ‘Explorer’ reaches Mylavaram forest near Vijayawada; four villages on alert
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: GPS-enabled collar helps forest officials track the movement; no attacks on cattle or human habitations reported so far

The tiger ‘Explorer’, which has been roaming across the Eastern Ghats after travelling through several States, has entered the Mylavaram forest range in the Vijayawada forest division and was seen in the A. Konduru forest block on Friday (November 20, 2026), triggering a fresh alert among forest officials.

The tiger is staying in a hilly stretch with thick forest cover and dense bush growth. Forest officials are tracking its movements with the help of a GPS-enabled satellite radio collar fitted to it following its capture and subsequent release into the Papikondalu National Park earlier this year. Officials said the tiger had not entered any human habitation so far and no cattle deaths or attacks on livestock had been reported in the Mylavaram range.
The villages of A. Konduru, Cheemalapadu, Vinagadapa and Narkulapadu, located in the vicinity of the forest block, have been alerted as a precautionary measure.

Forest personnel are monitoring the animal's movements and keeping a safe distance to avoid disturbing it. Officials said its movement was being tracked continuously, though its next direction of travel could not be predicted.

The tiger was first noticed in the Nuzvidu range a couple of days ago and moved towards the Mylavaram range overnight. It has been staying in the A. Konduru forest block since the following morning. Officials said it could move back towards Nuzvidu or proceed towards other forest stretches, depending on its movement.

articles.title: Millions of students take NEET, yet hundreds of medical seats go vacant
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Under the 2026 Float and Freeze option, candidates can carry forward their allotments without completing admission formalities, and even if their seats remain unchanged in Round 3, they can choose not to join; this flexibility has had significant implications in seat utilisation

Even as millions of candidates competed for admission, several undergraduate MBBS seats remained vacant during the NEET-UG 2026 counselling. Over 3,000-3,400 vacancies were reported after the initial All India Quota (AIQ) and State rounds, with approximately 410 seats still unfilled in deemed universities even after the Special Stray Vacancy Round.
(Sign up for THEdge , The Hindu’s weekly education newsletter.)

While government medical college seats were all filled, most remaining vacancies were in deemed universities. States such as Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karnataka accounted for a significant share of these vacancies, raising concerns about high fees, seat utilisation and equitable access to medical education.

As per the data published by the National Medical Commission (NMC), the total number of MBBS seats available in the country for the academic session 2026–27 stands at 1,40,664. Of these, 64,121 seats are available in government medical colleges, while the remaining 76,543 seats are in the private medical sector. The latter comprises 14,299 seats in deemed university medical colleges and 62,244 seats in self-financing private medical colleges. Thus, more than 54% of the total MBBS seats in the country are concentrated in the private medical sector, where the cost of medical education is generally substantially higher than in government institutions.

The National Testing Agency (NTA) reported that 11,21,185 candidates qualified NEET-UG 2026 by securing marks above the prescribed category-wise qualifying cut-off. This included 9,96,935 candidates belonging to the General/EWS qualifying category, and 1,24,250 candidates belonging to the OBC, SC and ST categories who qualified with scores ranging from 177 to 212 marks.

articles.title: Cheetah brought from Botswana gives birth to four cubs at Kuno
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: With these four new arrivals, India’s cheetah population has risen to 62, including 43 Indian-born individuals

A two-and-a-half-year-old cheetah, KOMG 3, brought from Botswana, gave birth to four healthy cubs in the wild at Madhya Pradesh’s Kuno National Park on Friday (November 20, 2026), Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav said.
Calling the development a matter of pride for Madhya Pradesh and the entire country, Chief Minister Mohan Yadav said it was a historic achievement for Project Cheetah.
In a post on X, Bhupender Yadav said KOMG 3 is the first cheetah from Botswana to give birth in India.
“This is a landmark moment for Project Cheetah and a proud milestone in India’s journey towards restoring a viable cheetah population,” he added.
This is the second recorded birth in the wild since the reintroduction programme began in 2022.
With these four new arrivals, India’s cheetah population has risen to 62, including 43 Indian-born individuals.
“Every such birth strengthens our hope, deepens our commitment, and reminds us that conservation is a journey of patience, perseverance and collective effort,” Mr. Yadav said.
He also acknowledged the dedication, commitment and hard work of project managers, veterinarians, frontline forest staff and everyone working tirelessly for the success of Project Cheetah.

In a statement, CM Mohan Yadav said, “This is a matter of pride for Madhya Pradesh and the entire country. The birth of cubs in India for the first time by a female cheetah from Botswana is a historic achievement of Project Cheetah.

“This is an important and encouraging step towards restoring a viable cheetah population in India. KOMG 3, a female cheetah, gave birth to four healthy cubs in natural conditions after spending more than four months in the wild.”

With these four new arrivals, India’s cheetah population has risen to 62, including 43 Indian-born individuals

A two-and-a-half-year-old cheetah, KOMG 3, brought from Botswana, gave birth to four healthy cubs in the wild at Madhya Pradesh’s Kuno National Park on Friday (November 20, 2026), Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav said.

Calling the development a matter of pride for Madhya Pradesh and the entire country, Chief Minister Mohan Yadav said it was a historic achievement for Project Cheetah.

In a post on X, Bhupender Yadav said KOMG 3 is the first cheetah from Botswana to give birth in India.

“This is a landmark moment for Project Cheetah and a proud milestone in India’s journey towards restoring a viable cheetah population,” he added.

This is the second recorded birth in the wild since the reintroduction programme began in 2022.

With these four new arrivals, India’s cheetah population has risen to 62, including 43 Indian-born individuals.

“Every such birth strengthens our hope, deepens our commitment, and reminds us that conservation is a journey of patience, perseverance and collective effort,” Mr. Yadav said.

He also acknowledged the dedication, commitment and hard work of project managers, veterinarians, frontline forest staff and everyone working tirelessly for the success of Project Cheetah.

In a statement, CM Mohan Yadav said, “This is a matter of pride for Madhya Pradesh and the entire country. The birth of cubs in India for the first time by a female cheetah from Botswana is a historic achievement of Project Cheetah.

“This is an important and encouraging step towards restoring a viable cheetah population in India. KOMG 3, a female cheetah, gave birth to four healthy cubs in natural conditions after spending more than four months in the wild.”

fullParagraphs: India’s cheetah population has risen to 52, including 32 cubs born in the country, as Project Cheetah completes four years on September 17, 2026, with officials highlighting the survival of cubs, breeding success and the expansion of the animals into open forest areas as key milestones.
Cheetah brought from Botswana gives birth to four cubs at Kuno
On September 17, 2022, Prime Minister Narendra Modi released eight wild cheetahs from Namibia into special enclosures at Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh.
The next phase of the cheetah restoration programme involves expanding suitable habitat for cheetahs and establishing a comprehensive, long term cheetah meta population in India.

While 49 cheetahs are in Kuno National Park, three others are in Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary, both in Madhya Pradesh. Over the last four years, many important milestones have been achieved, ranging from the reintroduction of cheetahs to breeding, survival of cubs and expansion into open forest, an official said in a statement.
The journey that began in Namibia on the distant African continent has now reached Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary. A total of 32 cheetahs were born in India, officials said.

The success in cheetah breeding and expansion was achieved by learning from difficulties. “The team faced many challenges in the first year of cheetah reintroduction. During this time, they gained experience in cheetah behaviour, health, and management adapted to Indian conditions,” an official said.
In the next year, the focus shifted to the survival and development of cubs born in India. According to the document, 13 cubs survived for more than a year after birth.

In the third year, 2025, cheetahs were released into open forest areas. They were monitored 24 hours a day across an interstate landscape spanning 12 districts, officials said, adding that the cheetahs gradually adapted to new areas.
The establishment of breeding females and the successful survival of the second generation of cubs in the fourth year are considered significant achievements of the programme, they said.

articles.title: Digital planetariums, education centres will be established in all divisions: Bihar Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Requisition for appointment of 1,061 faculty posts for Engineering Colleges and 354 faculty posts for polytechnic colleges sent to BPSC

With a view to developing a scientific temperament among students and the general public, state-of-the-art “digital planetariums and education centres” will be established in all the divisions of the state, Bihar Science and Technology Minister Sheela Kumari said on Friday (November 20, 2026).
“The district magistrates of the districts concerned have been requested to provide a minimum of two acres of land for the purpose,” Ms. Kumari said while addressing a press conference in Patna.

These centres will provide children and young people with practical knowledge of astronomy and space research, she said, while praising Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary’s leadership for the initiative.
In reply to a query, she said that these planetariums will be ready in a year.

The Minister further stated that digital planetariums/space and astronomy education centres will also be established in three districts—East Champaran, Jamui, and Purnea—as part of the Union Ministry of Culture’s Scheme for Promotion of Culture and Science (SPOCS).

“The total estimated project cost is ₹39.00 crore, which will be funded with central assistance,” she said, adding that the target is to commence construction work during the current financial year, 2026-27.

A digital planetarium uses computer software and high-resolution digital projectors (or LED panels) to display 3D simulations of the night sky, space travel, and science visuals inside a dome theatre. Unlike traditional optical-mechanical projectors that only show fixed star positions, digital systems can fly viewers through galaxies, simulate different time periods, and play full-dome films.
Ms. Kumari was accompanied by Department Secretary Himanshu Sharma and a host of other senior officials during the press conference.

In order to generate public interest in science and technology, efforts are also being made to operate mobile science exhibition buses, observatory domes, and astro parks through the National Council of Science Museums.

Notably, the state currently has two functional planetariums—one each in Patna and Darbhanga. The planetarium in Darbhanga was established in 2023, while the renovation of the Patna planetarium has already been completed.

articles.title: BJP’s invitation to Pakistan’s Minister vindicates Abdullah’s stance: J&K Deputy Chief Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: People’s Democratic Party legislator Muntazir Mehdi termed the Pakistani Minister’s visit to India “a welcome development” and urged the resumption of dialogue between India and Pakistan

J&K Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary on Friday (November 20, 2026) said that the BJP-led government’s move to invite Pakistan’s Minister Musadik Masood Malik to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisation Dialogue Forum “vindicated the stand of National Conference (NC) president Dr. Farooq Abdullah and vice president Omar Abdullah.”

Referring to the BJP’s stance after the 2025 Pahalgam attack, Mr. Choudhary said, “The BJP will say it will not talk to Pakistan. And when Dr. Abdullah and Omar Abdullah advocate dialogue, the BJP will call them Pakistani. I want to ask the BJP: hasn’t a Pakistani Minister been invited to India on their invitation?”

He said the invitation to the Pakistani Minister proved that “the stance of my leaders was right then and is right now.” “The NC’s stance is the same as the one articulated by former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, who would say, ‘You can choose your friends, but you cannot choose your neighbours.’ One must always maintain good relations with one’s neighbours,” said Mr. Choudhary.

Asking Pakistan to end terrorism, Mr. Choudhary said, “Both Dr. Abdullah and Omar Abdullah have been asking Pakistan to end terrorism and close terror camps if Pakistan wants better relations. We stand behind our leaders.”
People’s Democratic Party legislator Muntazir Mehdi termed the Pakistani Minister’s visit to India “a welcome development” and urged the resumption of dialogue between India and Pakistan.

“The two countries share a common history and several mutual concerns, including political issues, climate change, and water-related matters, which can only be addressed through engagement and dialogue. Hostility and non-engagement cannot resolve these issues. Both countries should come to the table and resume dialogue for peace and development in the subcontinent,” he said.

People’s Democratic Party legislator Muntazir Mehdi termed the Pakistani Minister’s visit to India “a welcome development” and urged the resumption of dialogue between India and Pakistan

J&K Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary on Friday (November 20, 2026) said that the BJP-led government’s move to invite Pakistan’s Minister Musadik Masood Malik to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisation Dialogue Forum “vindicated the stand of National Conference (NC) president Dr. Farooq Abdullah and vice president Omar Abdullah.”

Referring to the BJP’s stance after the 2025 Pahalgam attack, Mr. Choudhary said, “The BJP will say it will not talk to Pakistan. And when Dr. Abdullah and Omar Abdullah advocate dialogue, the BJP will call them Pakistani. I want to ask the BJP: hasn’t a Pakistani Minister been invited to India on their invitation?”

He said the invitation to the Pakistani Minister proved that “the stance of my leaders was right then and is right now.” “The NC’s stance is the same as the one articulated by former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, who would say, ‘You can choose your friends, but you cannot choose your neighbours.’ One must always maintain good relations with one’s neighbours,” said Mr. Choudhary.

Asking Pakistan to end terrorism, Mr. Choudhary said, “Both Dr. Abdullah and Omar Abdullah have been asking Pakistan to end terrorism and close terror camps if Pakistan wants better relations. We stand behind our leaders.”

People’s Democratic Party legislator Muntazir Mehdi termed the Pakistani Minister’s visit to India “a welcome development” and urged the resumption of dialogue between India and Pakistan.

“The two countries share a common history and several mutual concerns, including political issues, climate change, and water-related matters, which can only be addressed through engagement and dialogue. Hostility and non-engagement cannot resolve these issues. Both countries should come to the table and resume dialogue for peace and development in the subcontinent,” he said.

articles.title: Transgender persons to be roped in for tax collection in West Bengal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: West Bengal Minister Agnimitra Paul launches a programme to provide dignified, alternative livelihoods to trans persons

The West Bengal government will engage transgender persons to collect municipal tax and spread traffic awareness. Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Minister Agnimitra Paul said the initiative, called “Brihannala Brigade”, will provide an opportunity for a dignified livelihood for the transpersons.

“The CM wishes that they (transgender people no) longer have to resort to begging at traffic signals; instead, we want to offer them an alternative, respectable livelihood. We have decided that those among them who are interested will receive training from the police and be deployed at traffic signals. Their role will be to sensitise the public about traffic rules and safety measures,” Ms. Paul said on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

She further added that another group of transgender persons would be trained to collect outstanding taxes, which could help address the staff shortage that leads to delayed collections and large pending amounts.

The Minister also added that each of these transgender individuals will be provided with training to engage in this work so that they can conduct better public interaction and do their work seamlessly. They will receive a stipend for the work, Ms. Paul said.

The West Bengal government has started an initiative to offer relief in paying outstanding property taxes, including in the actual sums and interest, to encourage defaulters to pay their outstanding balances.
According to Kolkata Municipal Corporation estimates, they have around ₹6800 crore outstanding property tax pending, including personal properties, mixed-use properties, and commercial properties.

In 2022, the previous Mamata Banerjee government decided to allow transgender persons to apply for government jobs under the general category to help them have better opportunities in employment. A Transgender Development Board was set up in 2017, but the board could not undertake many activities for the welfare of members of the community. The last census carried out in the state in 2011 put the number of transgender people in the state at 30,349. The actual number of people of the third gender may be higher, several groups working for the community say.

articles.title: Trinamool supporters attacked outside the police station as police questioned Abhishek
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The supporters of Trinamool had gathered outside the police station in support of Abhishek Banerjee

Supporters of Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) were allegedly attacked on Friday (November 20, 2026) by supporters of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) outside a police station while party leader Abhishek Banerjee was being questioned by Kolkata Police at the Girish Park police station.

Videos of the scuffle and the assault on women supporters of the Trinamool were shared on social media and by the Mamata AITC. In the videos, groups of women alleged to be BJP supporters were seen chasing another group of women. Supporters of the Trinamool had gathered outside the police station in support of Abhishek Banerjee. The BJP leaders denied allegations of the assault but claimed that Trinamool supporters were trying to incite tensions by gathering outside the police station.

“@BJP4Bengal workers gathered outside Girish Park Police Station today, seemingly intent on harassing, heckling and assaulting our workers, did not even spare ordinary citizens and parents who had come to pick up their children from school,” the party shared on social media. The Mamata AITC leader raised questions on the role of politics.

The police complaint against the Diamond Harbour MP was filed in connection with remarks reportedly made by him on 29 October, in which he criticised sections of the police administration, alleging that officers were acting under political pressure. Mr. Banerjee took to social media to share videos of BJP leaders, including Suvendu Adhikari, alleging threats to the police when they were in the Opposition.

After the BJP came to power, several FIRs were registered against Abhishek Banerjee. He has been summoned to appear before the police on numerous occasions. Later in the day, the Trinamool leader filed a Zero FIR at Girish Park Police Station, highlighting how Suvendu Adhikari, Dilip Ghosh, and other BJP leaders threatened the Kolkata Police and the West Bengal Police on multiple occasions.

“The expertise and urgency shown by Girish Park PS in connection with Abhishek Banerjee’s matter—we hope the same expertise and urgency will be shown by them in connection with this Zero FIR, and that they will investigate the matter,” Arka Nag, an advocate representing Trinamool Congress leader, said.

articles.title: Anthropic researcher says Claude solved maths’ greatest riddle
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics

A mathematician at AI company Anthropic said Friday (November 20, 2026) that he had used the firm’s Claude chatbot to prove the Riemann Hypothesis, a problem that has eluded mathematicians for more than 160 years.
“I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Levent Alpoge wrote in a four-page note released Friday (November 20, 2026).
The claim has not been independently verified, and the proof has not yet been reviewed by outside experts.

First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics.
It is one of seven Millennium Prize Problems selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute in 2000, which offers $1 million for a solution to each.
Under the institute’s rules, a solution must be published in a peer-reviewed journal and withstand two years of scrutiny.
Mr. Alpoge said the method also resolves a broader version of the problem known as the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis.

He said he and Claude had produced a version of the proof in Lean, a programming language that allows mathematical arguments to be checked by a computer, and that he was releasing only that version for now.
A full written argument would be extremely long, he said, adding that he had not yet mastered all of the mathematics involved and planned to write it up properly.

Mr. Alpoge said he had consulted Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei before announcing the result and acknowledged that its timing could be viewed cynically, without elaborating, though he was probably referring to this week’s record IPO.
