articles.title: Outlook outage: On Microsoft and dangers of centralising digital systems
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The dangers of centralising the internet’s architecture are now clear

Last week, Microsoft’s suite of productivity and email software, which businesses, governments, hospitals and a host of other organisations rely upon round-the-clock, abruptly stopped working globally , affecting tens of millions of people around the world. The company has cited a network upgrade gone awry as the root cause of the incident. Incidents such as the Microsoft 365 outage are a natural consequence of businesses and governments allowing key digital systems to become centralised all over the world. The internet remains, and was pioneered as, a network of networks. If one business’s networks went down, the reasoning went, others would not fall like dominos: everyone was, after all, connected to everyone else. But the economics have long been prohibitive, with dedicated servers and web-connected infrastructure infeasible for all but the largest businesses, with even those firms seeking the enticing cost savings from socialised infrastructure. That made sense: the internet made shared infrastructure more economical, allowing hardware and maintenance costs to be spread so far and wide that at a per-user level prices have been negligible. Competition among major cloud providers, the few that remain at Microsoft’s scale, have kept prices affordable for enterprise software for all shades of organisations.

Digital services have grown more sophisticated, and more deeply integrated into the economy as this centralisation unfolded. But the downside is that, regardless of the sophistication and professionalism of any company, mistakes happen, and the scale of these mistakes can quickly cascade over to the entire economy. There are societal and organisational lessons to be gleaned from these episodes. There is no such thing as a reliable vendor. Governments must also draw a cyber sovereignty lesson here that does not simply entail swapping a global vendor for a domestic one. It is the subversion of the internet’s architecture that is at the root of these incidents. Investing in resilience — and shielding critical operations from destabilising disruptions, no matter how improbable — should inform attitudes to digital systems. As a new generation of AI data centres is poised to supercharge the centralised systems of yesteryear, it is all the more imperative to mitigate even occasional vagaries of large systems.

Editorial Context: Outlook outage: On Microsoft and dangers of centralising digital systems. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

The dangers of centralising the internet’s architecture are now clear

Last week, Microsoft’s suite of productivity and email software, which businesses, governments, hospitals and a host of other organisations rely upon round-the-clock, abruptly stopped working globally , affecting tens of millions of people around the world. The company has cited a network upgrade gone awry as the root cause of the incident. Incidents such as the Microsoft 365 outage are a natural consequence of businesses and governments allowing key digital systems to become centralised all over the world. The internet remains, and was pioneered as, a network of networks. If one business’s networks went down, the reasoning went, others would not fall like dominos: everyone was, after all, connected to everyone else. But the economics have long been prohibitive, with dedicated servers and web-connected infrastructure infeasible for all but the largest businesses, with even those firms seeking the enticing cost savings from socialised infrastructure. That made sense: the internet made shared infrastructure more economical, allowing hardware and maintenance costs to be spread so far and wide that at a per-user level prices have been negligible. Competition among major cloud providers, the few that remain at Microsoft’s scale, have kept prices affordable for enterprise software for all shades of organisations.

Digital services have grown more sophisticated, and more deeply integrated into the economy as this centralisation unfolded. But the downside is that, regardless of the sophistication and professionalism of any company, mistakes happen, and the scale of these mistakes can quickly cascade over to the entire economy. There are societal and organisational lessons to be gleaned from these episodes. There is no such thing as a reliable vendor. Governments must also draw a cyber sovereignty lesson here that does not simply entail swapping a global vendor for a domestic one. It is the subversion of the internet’s architecture that is at the root of these incidents. Investing in resilience — and shielding critical operations from destabilising disruptions, no matter how improbable — should inform attitudes to digital systems. As a new generation of AI data centres is poised to supercharge the centralised systems of yesteryear, it is all the more imperative to mitigate even occasional vagaries of large systems.

articles.title: Clear the path: On SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India should use multilateral fora to advance bilateral cooperation

While maintaining its hard stance on cross-border terrorism, India has an opportunity to recognise that many of its other interests still merit sustained cooperation with Pakistan as the latter’s climate minister Musadik Masood Malik prepares to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi. India’s official position since the Pahalgam attack and the ensuing confrontations along the border is that terrorism and bilateral talks cannot coexist. A month later, Prime Minister Narendra Modi signalled that India’s relations with Pakistan would remain subordinate to its demands on cross-border terrorism by extending the condition to trade and water. South Asia is already one of the least economically integrated regions worldwide, with intra-regional trade at around 5%, and, as Chatham House has inferred, strained ties between India and its neighbours have created diplomatic vacuums that Beijing has taken advantage of through trilateral and regional groupings. Now, by inviting all SCO members to the national capital and participating in meetings ahead of the August 2027 Islamabad Summit, New Delhi has shown some maturity as a convening power. Islamabad is also being pragmatic in keeping channels open during its SCO chairmanship by participating in an initiative championed by Mr. Modi.

The pursuit of regionwide water security remains particularly fluid, with India seemingly overlooking the fact that it is upstream of Pakistan and Bangladesh and downstream of China. After India stopped sharing routine hydrological data of the Indus river and approved the Chenab-Beas link tunnel project, Mr. Malik fanned the flames saying Pakistan would “cut off those hands” seeking to restrict its share of the water. Yet China has now restricted the same data vis-à-vis the Brahmaputra while it builds the Medog mega-dam in Tibet. India has also protested the proposed Padma Barrage in Bangladesh, which has been increasing its alignment with China, echoing India building the Farakka Barrage over East Pakistan’s objections in 1961. Climate change is rendering cooperation more essential to manage the integrity of contested geographies, the willingness of border populations to engage, and the potential to generate hydroelectric power. New Delhi should retreat from the notion that working together on the Indus will be a concession to Islamabad and see in the Dialogue an opportunity to restore the necessary channels. Suspending ties may communicate political resolve but will not diminish terrorists’ capabilities in the region or improve India’s security. It has already compromised India’s ambitions to regional leadership, which require the ability to keep engaging even with difficult neighbours. India should go beyond using multilateral fora to assert its national position and start identifying areas where bilateral cooperation serves its interests, including with Pakistan.

Editorial Context: Clear the path: On SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

articles.title: 10 patented technologies handed over to various firms at T.N. Tech Transfer Summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Inaugurating the Summit, P. Viswanathan, Higher Education Minister, says it will be made into an annual affair and will be taken to other major cities in Tamil Nadu as well

Students of Classes VII and IX of the Coimbatore Public School have developed a fruit harvesting toolkit for coffee cherries. On Thursday, their innovation, for which they have applied for a patent on June 25, 2026, was passed on to a start-up firm for commercialisation.

The toolkit has a hollow pipe attached to a harvesting head that has a set of blades to cut off the ripe coffee cherries. The set of blades arranged in V-shape are guided by a push-pull casting while harvesting. The picked cherries glide through the hollow flexible hose into a storage container. The purpose of the innovation was to increase the efficiency and speed of fruit harvesting operations in plantations. This was one of the 10 products for which technology transfer took place at the Tamil Nadu Technology Transfer Summit 2006, organised jointly by the Tamil Nadu State Council for Science and Technology (TNSCST) and Anna University.

S.A. Nirmala, correspondent, Coimbatore Public School, said that every year, the students work on a real-life problem that is brought in either by parents or the community. This prototype was the product of one such problem brought in by a parent. The technology was transferred to Nexorasai Pvt. Ltd., a startup firm started by the parent. Before the handover, students tested the prototype at a coffee plantation for efficacy, she said.

Among the new innovations are a drone-based infrastructure cleaning system developed by Anna University, a sanitary napkin vending machine developed by VIT Chennai, foxtail millet cookies technology, millet muesli, banana stem juice, and low-fat dessicated coconut chips technology.

S. Vincent, member secretary, TNSCST, said a total of 97 innovative technologies had emerged from higher education institutions in the State which were ready to be transferred for commercialisation. While only 10 technologies were transferred to start-ups and MSMEs for commercialisation, at least 60 industry representatives had participated at the Summit and had shown interest in the innovations.

Inaugurating the Summit, P. Viswanathan, Higher Education Minister, said it would be made into an annual affair and would be taken to other major cities in Tamil Nadu as well. He released a book titled A Compendium of Registered Geographical Indications of Tamil Nadu documenting the State’s heritage of traditional products and indigenous knowledge.

Inaugurating the Summit, P. Viswanathan, Higher Education Minister, says it will be made into an annual affair and will be taken to other major cities in Tamil Nadu as well

Students of Classes VII and IX of the Coimbatore Public School have developed a fruit harvesting toolkit for coffee cherries. On Thursday, their innovation, for which they have applied for a patent on June 25, 2026, was passed on to a start-up firm for commercialisation.

The toolkit has a hollow pipe attached to a harvesting head that has a set of blades to cut off the ripe coffee cherries. The set of blades arranged in V-shape are guided by a push-pull casting while harvesting. The picked cherries glide through the hollow flexible hose into a storage container. The purpose of the innovation was to increase the efficiency and speed of fruit harvesting operations in plantations. This was one of the 10 products for which technology transfer took place at the Tamil Nadu Technology Transfer Summit 2006, organised jointly by the Tamil Nadu State Council for Science and Technology (TNSCST) and Anna University.

S.A. Nirmala, correspondent, Coimbatore Public School, said that every year, the students work on a real-life problem that is brought in either by parents or the community. This prototype was the product of one such problem brought in by a parent. The technology was transferred to Nexorasai Pvt. Ltd., a startup firm started by the parent. Before the handover, students tested the prototype at a coffee plantation for efficacy, she said.

Among the new innovations are a drone-based infrastructure cleaning system developed by Anna University, a sanitary napkin vending machine developed by VIT Chennai, foxtail millet cookies technology, millet muesli, banana stem juice, and low-fat dessicated coconut chips technology.

S. Vincent, member secretary, TNSCST, said a total of 97 innovative technologies had emerged from higher education institutions in the State which were ready to be transferred for commercialisation. While only 10 technologies were transferred to start-ups and MSMEs for commercialisation, at least 60 industry representatives had participated at the Summit and had shown interest in the innovations.

articles.title: Dr. NTRUHS plans AI-based courses in affiliated colleges to strengthen research collaboration
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The university examining the feasibility of introducing interdisciplinary certificate and diploma programmes in emerging areas of health sciences

Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences (NTRUHS) is planning to introduce new academic programmes incorporating Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML), while strengthening research collaboration among its affiliated medical colleges.
The proposals were discussed at a meeting of principals, academic vice-principals and research committee members of affiliated medical colleges, held at the university on Thursday.

Vice-Chancellor P. Chandrasekhar said medical education must keep pace with technological advancements and changing healthcare needs. He said medical institutions should take advantage of the opportunities emerging from the State’s technology initiatives by working closely with engineering colleges, research organisations and industry.

The meeting discussed a proposal to establish a university-wide Research and Innovation Network by bringing together research facilities and the Department of Health Research and Indian Council of Medical Research-supported Multidisciplinary Research Units (MRUs) functioning in affiliated medical colleges.

The proposed network would help institutions share expertise, undertake collaborative and multicentric research projects and address healthcare challenges through coordinated research efforts, according to a release by the university.
The university is also examining the feasibility of introducing interdisciplinary certificate and diploma programmes in emerging areas of health sciences.

The meeting also discussed the proposed Amaravati School of Bio-Design, which seeks to bring medical professionals, engineers, researchers and technology institutions onto a common platform to develop innovative healthcare solutions.

The initiative is envisaged as part of the emerging innovation ecosystem associated with Amaravati Quantum Valley and Bio Valley. It would focus on identifying real-world healthcare problems and developing solutions through biomedical design, engineering and technology, the participants discussed.
The school has been proposed at the Vivenns campus in Mayuri Tech Park, Mangalagiri, with its inauguration planned for December 7, 2026.
Possibilities for collaboration with IIT Tirupati and other technical institutions were also discussed, particularly in biomedical research, medical device development and healthcare technology.

articles.title: Akvan may spare most of Andhra Pradesh; red alert issued for Srikakulam, Vizianagaram
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Parvathipuram-Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Anakapalli districts may record isolated very heavy rainfall till Friday evening, says IMD

Even as the severe cyclonic storm Akvan may spare most of Andhra Pradesh and make landfall along the south Odisha coast near Gopalpur on November 20, the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Amaravati, has put the Srikakulam and Vizianagaram districts bordering Odisha on a red alert.

Between 8.30 a.m. and 7 p.m. on Thursday, many weather stations in Srikakulam district recorded only light to moderate rain of below 35 mm. However, IMD, Amaravati, Director K. Naga Ratnam told The Hindu that the rainfall may increase from the midnight and may continue till Friday noon or evening. Isolated extremely heavy rainfall is likely in these two districts.

Gales of 90 kmph to 100 kmph are also likely along the coast in North Coastal Andhra Pradesh around the midnight. Already, strong winds of 50 kmph to 60 kmph are prevailing along the coast, the Director said.

Parvathipuram-Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Anakapalli districts may also record isolated very heavy rainfall till Friday evening, but the rest of the State may not see any rainfall activity on Friday.

Weather experts said while the weather system may move closer to the coast near Gopalpur in Odisha, which is around 180 km from Srikakulam, there is a slight possibility of the system making landfall near the extreme end of North Coastal Andhra Pradesh as well.

Meanwhile, as per the latest bulletin issued by the IMD at 5.30 p.m., Akvan moved northwards with the speed of 13 kmph till 2.30 p.m. and remained over the west-central Bay of Bengal, which is about 390 km east-southeast of Narsapur and 320 km south-southeast of Kalingapatnam of Andhra Pradesh, 410 km south of Gopalpur and 470 km south of Puri of Odisha and 610 km east-northeast of Chennai of Tamil Nadu.
It is likely to move north-northwestwards and cross the coast close to Gopalpur by Friday noon, with the maximum sustained wind speed of 90kmph to 100 kmph, gusting to 110 kmph.

A storm surge of 0.5 to 1.0 metre height above the astronomical tide is very likely to inundate low-lying areas along the coastal belt in the districts of Kakinada, Vizianagaram, Srikakulam and Visakhapatnam districts, the IMD said in its bulletin.

Parvathipuram-Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Anakapalli districts may record isolated very heavy rainfall till Friday evening, says IMD

Even as the severe cyclonic storm Akvan may spare most of Andhra Pradesh and make landfall along the south Odisha coast near Gopalpur on November 20, the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Amaravati, has put the Srikakulam and Vizianagaram districts bordering Odisha on a red alert.

Between 8.30 a.m. and 7 p.m. on Thursday, many weather stations in Srikakulam district recorded only light to moderate rain of below 35 mm. However, IMD, Amaravati, Director K. Naga Ratnam told The Hindu that the rainfall may increase from the midnight and may continue till Friday noon or evening. Isolated extremely heavy rainfall is likely in these two districts.

Gales of 90 kmph to 100 kmph are also likely along the coast in North Coastal Andhra Pradesh around the midnight. Already, strong winds of 50 kmph to 60 kmph are prevailing along the coast, the Director said.

Parvathipuram-Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Anakapalli districts may also record isolated very heavy rainfall till Friday evening, but the rest of the State may not see any rainfall activity on Friday.

Weather experts said while the weather system may move closer to the coast near Gopalpur in Odisha, which is around 180 km from Srikakulam, there is a slight possibility of the system making landfall near the extreme end of North Coastal Andhra Pradesh as well.

Meanwhile, as per the latest bulletin issued by the IMD at 5.30 p.m., Akvan moved northwards with the speed of 13 kmph till 2.30 p.m. and remained over the west-central Bay of Bengal, which is about 390 km east-southeast of Narsapur and 320 km south-southeast of Kalingapatnam of Andhra Pradesh, 410 km south of Gopalpur and 470 km south of Puri of Odisha and 610 km east-northeast of Chennai of Tamil Nadu.

It is likely to move north-northwestwards and cross the coast close to Gopalpur by Friday noon, with the maximum sustained wind speed of 90kmph to 100 kmph, gusting to 110 kmph.

A storm surge of 0.5 to 1.0 metre height above the astronomical tide is very likely to inundate low-lying areas along the coastal belt in the districts of Kakinada, Vizianagaram, Srikakulam and Visakhapatnam districts, the IMD said in its bulletin.

articles.title: Repository to catalogue research occurring at institutions in T.N. to be set up, says Higher Education Secretary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: He announces that Anna University has been asked to take the lead in developing this digital platform

The Tamil Nadu Higher Education Department will soon be starting a central digital repository of all research and innovation that are taking place in higher education institutions in the State, Higher Education Secretary Dheeraj Kumar said on Thursday.

Speaking at the Tamil Nadu Technology Transfer Summit 2026 organised jointly by the Tamil Nadu State Council for Science and Technology (TNSCST) and Anna University, Mr. Kumar said the repository would serve as a platform that would link various universities and institutions carrying out research and innovation in various fields, the industry, and the governmental and non-governmental organisations working with the innovators.

Later, elaborating on the initiative, he told The Hindu , “Development of technology generally gets spurred by a problem statement. Instead of doing the research ab initio , it is possible that some research would have already happened in certain universities of our State or some research institutions or centres that will be relevant to the solution that is now being sought. The point is to connect them.”

Mr. Kumar said Anna University had been asked to take the lead in developing the digital platform. “They have three incubation centres. We thought of looking at the domains that are industry-oriented that can be pushed first,” he added.

The initiative will entail the creation of a portal where all research work being carried out in universities and research institutions and innovative pursuits at incubation centres would be catalogued and put up. It will act as a common interface for stakeholders involved in the State’s innovation journey, from incubation to commercialisation, said V. Kumaresan, Registrar-in-charge, Anna University.

Explaining further, he said if a business house or a start-up firm is looking for a specific technology or process, instead of running from pillar to post they could visit the portal and tap into the research work being carried out by institutions across the State. “It will help the State to identify areas where we are s t rong, research areas where the universities are working, and the possible avenues for innovation,” Dr. Kumaresan added.

articles.title: Tension in Pulivendula for third day as TDP, YSRCP spar over ‘poll violence’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tense moments prevailed for the third consecutive day in the Pulivendula constituency of Kadapa district on Thursday as Telugu Desam Party (TDP) in-charge Mareddy Ravindranath Reddy, popularly known as ‘B.Tech Ravi’, staged a two-hour demonstration at the Pulivendula police station.

Accompanied by Member of the Legislative Council (MLC) Bhumireddy Ramagopal Reddy and two individuals allegedly injured in rival attacks, Mr. Ravi staged a sit-in in front of the station demanding a thorough investigation into a recent spate of political violence.

The protest was triggered by violent incidents reported in Agudur (Chakrayapet mandal) and Malyala (Thondur mandal), where several TDP workers and their properties – including those belonging to Simhadripuram Market Committee Chairman Bandi Ramasubba Reddy – were targeted.
Earlier in the day, Mr. Ravi visited the sites where the two-wheelers of TDP candidates were reportedly set ablaze to inspect the burnt remains.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Ravi accused the police of inaction. “While individuals booked under Section 307 in firing cases are roaming freely on the streets, the police are turning a blind eye,” he alleged. “Despite video evidence showing these accused individuals moving alongside MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy, the department has taken no action.”
He further charged YSRCP leaders with driving tractors menacingly around nomination centres to intimidate voters and attempting to run them over TDP cadres.

Deputy Inspector-General of Police (Kurnool range) Koya Praveen, who had previously visited Pulivendula during the municipal elections to assure the safety of candidates and voters, intervened and offered to look into Mr. Ravi’s complaints once the nomination phase concludes.

Hitting back at the protest, Kadapa MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy dismissed the sit-in outside the police station as “a big drama” and advised the TDP leader to refrain from what he termed “cheap politics”. In a counter-allegation, Mr. Avinash Reddy accused the TDP leadership of orchestrating attacks on YSRCP cadres by misusing official machinery, claiming that Mr. Ravi was now attempting to distort the facts to garner public sympathy.

articles.title: Anthropic raises $81 billion in IPO amid AI market volatility
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The Claude maker priced its shares at $83 apiece, implying an equity valuation of about $1.03 trillion based on outstanding shares, with trading scheduled to begin on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on November 19

Anthropic, the maker of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot Claude, has priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 a share, valuing the offering at approximately $81.34 billion, according to an announcement by the company on November 18.

The company said its shares were expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19 under the ticker symbol ANT. The offering is expected to close on November 20, subject to customary closing conditions.

According to Anthropic’s announcement, the offering comprises 980 million shares of Class A common stock. Of these, 956.35 million shares are being sold by the company and 23.65 million by existing shareholders. Anthropic said it would not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares by the selling shareholders.

At the IPO price of $83 a share, the company’s portion of the offering is valued at approximately $79.38 billion, while the shares sold by existing shareholders are valued at approximately $1.96 billion. These figures are before underwriting discounts and expenses.
At $83 a share, Anthropic’s overall equity value works out to approximately $1.03 trillion, based on the total number of shares outstanding after the IPO.
Anthropic has also given the banks (underwriters) managing the IPO the option to purchase an additional 147 million shares within 30 days, potentially increasing the size of the offering.
Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are the lead underwriters for the IPO, with JPMorgan, Citigroup, Barclays and other investment banks also participating, according to the SEC filing.
The IPO comes amid growing investor concerns over the sustainability of the AI investment boom and whether technology companies can generate sufficient returns from their infrastructure spending.
On November 5, the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5%, wiping out trillions of dollars in market value, while NVIDIA shares declined 9% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 12%.

Earlier, on October 29, Alphabet shares plunged 12.6%, wiping out approximately $500 billion in market value after its quarterly results raised concerns over its advertising business and the cash-flow impact of rising AI investments. The sell-off reflected broader concerns over the valuations of AI-linked companies and the returns from their heavy spending on data centres and computing infrastructure.

fullParagraphs: The ECI offers relief to a section of deleted electors but SIR’s flaws remain

Following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in some States that had undergone the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) , mostly in Phases 1 and 2, some 74 lakh names were added onto the electoral rolls. This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Draft deletions in Phase 3 of the SIR averaged 17% , and reached 32.8% in Delhi . The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number.

These “corrective” measures follow the Supreme Court’s observation on October 28 that forcing deleted electors to re-enrol through Form 6, meant for new voters, was an “error”. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.

articles.title: Two months after deciding to drag the Centre to court, Maharashtra government decides to withdraw petition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe had challenged FSSAI over the constitutional validity of a few regulations. The petition had challenged the creation of a few posts by the Centre, claiming it was against the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006

Two months after deciding to drag the Centre to court over a jurisdiction dispute, the Maharashtra government has taken a call to withdraw its petition, which had accused the Central government of usurping its power and creating new rules in a ‘clandestine manner’.

On September 3, 2026, Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration had filed a petition against FSSAI, challenging the constitutional validity of a few regulations. It had claimed that these regulations had led to the creation of ‘a parallel structure’ which ‘encroached upon the powers and duties of the State Commissioner of Food Safety and his officers.’ On October 29, the government directed officials to withdraw this petition, which had caused a stir as it led to a tussle between the Centre and the State, both governed by the Bharatiya Janata Party.

Political & National Report: Two months after deciding to drag the Centre to court, Maharashtra government decides to withdraw petition. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.

articles.title: Emerging radicalisation hotspots now under purview of Multi-Agency Centre: Amit Shah
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Union Home Minister calls on anti-terrorism squads of every State to strengthen their cyber-expert units

The Multi-Agency Centre (MAC), a centralised intelligence-sharing platform, now tracks cybersecurity, narcotics, organised crime networks, and emerging radicalisation hotspots, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

The MAC, which also acts as a common counter-terrorism grid and functions under the Intelligence Bureau (IB), was conceptualised in 2001, in the aftermath of the Kargil war, but became fully operational in 2009.
In 2025, the MAC network was revamped to connect all police districts in the country through a secure network. Mr. Shah said that the functioning of the MAC has been reorganised.
He said that the anti-terrorism squads (ATS) of every State needed to strengthen their cyber-expert units as technology is increasingly being used in such crimes.

He made the remarks while addressing the inaugural session of the two-day counter-terrorism conference organised by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in New Delhi. On the occasion, he released the publication, Fail-Safe Investigation, brought out by the NIA. articles.title: Women in high public office doesn’t mean equality throughout society: Justice Nagarathna
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court judge says a woman may hold a senior position while other women remain excluded from education, employment, property, or effective legal remedies

Justice B.V. Nagarathna, one of the senior most judges of the Supreme Court and in line to be the first woman Chief Justice of India, has said that the mere existence of women in high public office does not establish that equality has been achieved throughout society.

“A woman may hold a senior position while other women remain excluded from education, employment, property, or effective legal remedies,” Justice Nagarathna said at the inaugural Cornelia Sorabji Memorial Lecture at Somerville College in the University of Oxford on Wednesday (November 18, 2026).
Only the practice of substantive equality could take care of these differences among women hailing from and living through diverse life experiences, the judge said.

Justice Nagarathna said a judgment cannot, by itself, guarantee that every workplace becomes safe, every girl receives education, every woman obtains her lawful inheritance, or every victim of domestic violence secures timely protection.
Likewise, legislation cannot achieve its full purpose if remedies were inaccessible, public authorities failed to act, or social attitudes prevent women from asserting their rights.

The judge said the enactment of Constitutional amendments which give women one-third of the seats in Parliament and the State legislatures was proof to show that women should participate in decision-making and not be content with just a formal right to vote.

“These developments reflect an important insight: where historical exclusion has shaped the composition of institutions, formal equality alone may not be sufficient to secure meaningful representation,” Justice Nagarathna pointed out.
Justice Nagarathna said that the progress of Indian women’s rights cannot be measured by the number of discriminatory provisions struck down or the enactment of a few beneficial laws.

The judge said recognition of violence against women as a violation of constitutional rights has not really translated in the real world to women seeking the protection of law without fear of stigma, retaliation or economic insecurity.

On the question of equality, Justice Nagarathna raised the fundamental problem of women being made to bear the “disproportionate burden of unpaid domestic and care work which continues to determine women’s choices”.

fullParagraphs: Director of Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre Manorama Mohanty said the duration of the landfall process would be a long process which could stretch over seven to eight hours

The land interaction commenced as the sheared cloud mass associated with the cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ entered into the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coasts early on Friday, says the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

“Latest satellite imagery indicates the land interaction commenced as the sheared cloud mass associated with the Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’ entered into the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coasts,” informed IMD on Friday (November 20, 2026).

The Severe Cyclonic Storm "Akvan" [Pronunciation: Akvan] over the westcentral Bay of Bengal moved north-northwestwards with the speed of 21 kmph during past 06 hours, weakened into a Cyclonic Storm and lay centered at 0230 hours IST of today, the 20th November, 2026 over the same region, near Latitude 17.7°N and Longitude 84.9°E, about 110 km southeast of Kalingapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 170 km east of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 170 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha), 250 km south-southwest of Puri (Odisha) and 370 km east-northeast of Narsapur (Andhra Pradesh). It is likely to continue to move north-northwestward and cross North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur, by forenoon of 20th November, 2026 with the maximum sustained wind speed of 70-80 kmph gusting to 90 kmph. Latest Satellite imagery indicates the Land interaction commenced as the sheared cloud mass associated with the Cyclonic Storm "Akvan" entered into north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coasts. The system is under continuous surveillance of the Doppler Weather Radar at Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur.

“The severe cyclonic storm Akvan over the westcentral Bay of Bengal moved north-northwestwards with the speed of 21 kmph during the past six hours, weakened into a cyclonic storm and lay centred over the same region about 110 km southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 170 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha) and 250 km south-southwest of Puri (Odisha),” informed the IMD bulletin.

“It is likely to continue to move north-northwestward and cross the North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur by the forenoon of November 20, 2026, with the maximum sustained wind speed of 70-80 kmph, gusting to 90 kmph,” it further said.

Director of Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre Manorama Mohanty said the duration of the landfall process would be a long process which could stretch over seven to eight hours. Meanwhile, coastal Odisha districts have started receiving heavy rain under the influence of the cyclone.

articles.title: Removal proceedings against me infructuous after resignation: Justice Varma tells Lok Sabha Secretariat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a letter circulated among MPs on November 19, Justice Varma stated that the proceedings directed toward his removal did not survive his resignation

Justice Yashwant Varma has contended that proceedings for his removal as a High Court judge became infructuous following his resignation and cannot be continued, saying any attempt to remove him from office would be without constitutional foundation.
In a letter dated September 10 to Lok Sabha Secretary General Utpal Kumar Singh, he responded to the report of the inquiry committee constituted by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla.
Mr. Varma wrote that the proceedings directed towards his removal did not survive his resignation.

He reiterated that he was innocent of the allegations against him, including the suggestion that he possessed ill-gotten funds, and asserted that his resignation should not be construed as an acknowledgement or admission of any allegation or finding.
The letter was circulated among MPs on Thursday (November 19, 2026).
The three-member inquiry committee, in its report tabled in Parliament on August 12, had found all three charges against Justice Varma proved .

The charges related to his failure to explain the presence, source or ownership of cash found at his official residence, failure to secure and preserve material evidence leading to the unexplained disappearance of the currency, and evasive and unsatisfactory explanations during the inquiry.

articles.title: Mahua Moitra alleges attack on her convoy by BJP supporters
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: BJP leaders said the alleged attack was Ms. Moitra’s attempt to gain attention and conduct self-promotion through social media live videos

Mamata All India Trinamool Congress lawmaker Mahua Moitra on Thursday (November 19, 2026) alleged that Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) members attacked her convoy when she was visiting her constituency — Krishnanagar — in Nadia district. She also accused the West Bengal police of inaction.

It is not the first time that the MP has been attacked since the BJP came to power in the State. “I have been attacked by the mob, with police waiting. My car was physically lifted. I have seen the same BJP member [I recognise his face] with flags,” Ms. Moitra said in a video statement after her car was attacked and vandalised.
She asked the Supreme Court, the Calcutta High Court, and the police to take note of the incident.

The Mamata loyalist also shared videos of BJP flags being carried by the mob that allegedly attacked her car and threw eggs at the windscreen. Ms. Moitra alleged that instead of rescuing her and neutralising the mob, the police personnel tried to stop her from attending her scheduled event in the area.
Meanwhile, Mamata's Trinamool general secretary Abhishek Banerjee and a Lok Sabha MP raised questions about the attack.

“Will the Calcutta High Court initiate contempt proceedings against the State Government and the Home Department for defying its orders, or does contempt of court apply only to the Opposition while those in power and their BJP allies enjoy special immunity?” Mr Banerjee asked.
West Bengal Industries Minister Tapas Roy said that without such incidents, Ms. Moitra does not get a chance to “go Live on Facebook”.

“She (Mahua Moitra) wants self-promotion. Now she does not have any other way of promotion, so these incidents are the only way for her to get some attention. If she wants, she can inform the court about any such incident,” Mr. Roy said.
On September 16, Ms. Moitra alleged that BJP workers pelted eggs on her during a visit to her Krishnanagar constituency in West Bengal’s Nadia.

articles.title: The Rohingya question: International solidarity, accountability and the missing road home
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The fundamental question remains: how does a community that has been systematically marginalised, displaced and denied its identity reclaim its place in the country it considers home?

The Rohingya question has returned to the centre of international attention following the landmark judgment delivered by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) on November 19, 2026. Yet, for more than a million Rohingya living outside Myanmar, legal recognition is only one part of a much larger struggle. The fundamental question remains: how does a community that has been systematically marginalised, displaced and denied its identity reclaim its place in the country it considers home? The crisis also exposes the international community’s inability to translate diplomatic declarations, humanitarian assistance and legal proceedings into a sustainable political settlement.

When I began working on Myanmar in the United Nations Department of Political Affairs in 2011, the Rohingya question was largely confined to perfunctory diplomatic talking points. Although concerns about discrimination, communal tensions and citizenship were acknowledged, there appeared to be limited understanding in many diplomatic discussions of the geographical and postcolonial nuances underlying the crisis.

This began to change with the outbreak of communal violence in May 2012, which dealt an early blow to Myanmar’s fragile democratisation process. The developments gradually compelled interlocutors to recognise that the country’s transition was not simply about moving away from military rule or introducing electoral reforms. It also involved confronting deeply entrenched postcolonial challenges, competing historical narratives, unresolved questions of identity and citizenship, and the complex relationship between the centre and its ethnic peripheries.

The Rohingya question could not be understood simply as another episode of communal tension between religious communities. It was deeply embedded in the history of colonial-era migration, the changing political geography of the Arakan region, competing narratives of belonging and the post-independence construction of citizenship in Myanmar. The historical relationship between the territories that now constitute Bangladesh and Myanmar, population movements during British colonial rule and the subsequent politicisation of identity were essential to understanding the dispute. The tendency to reduce the issue to a humanitarian concern or communal violence obscured these deeper historical and political dimensions.

🌐 International & Geopolitics 📅 20 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 The Rohingya question: International solidarity, accountability and the missing road home

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

The fundamental question remains: how does a community that has been systematically marginalised, displaced and denied its identity reclaim its place in the country it considers home?

The Rohingya question has returned to the centre of international attention following the landmark judgment delivered by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) on November 19, 2026. Yet, for more than a million Rohingya living outside Myanmar, legal recognition is only one part of a much larger struggle. The fundamental question remains: how does a community that has been systematically marginalised, displaced and denied its identity reclaim its place in the country it considers home? The crisis also exposes the international community’s inability to translate diplomatic declarations, humanitarian assistance and legal proceedings into a sustainable political settlement.

When I began working on Myanmar in the United Nations Department of Political Affairs in 2011, the Rohingya question was largely confined to perfunctory diplomatic talking points. Although concerns about discrimination, communal tensions and citizenship were acknowledged, there appeared to be limited understanding in many diplomatic discussions of the geographical and postcolonial nuances underlying the crisis.

This began to change with the outbreak of communal violence in May 2012, which dealt an early blow to Myanmar’s fragile democratisation process. The developments gradually compelled interlocutors to recognise that the country’s transition was not simply about moving away from military rule or introducing electoral reforms. It also involved confronting deeply entrenched postcolonial challenges, competing historical narratives, unresolved questions of identity and citizenship, and the complex relationship between the centre and its ethnic peripheries.

The Rohingya question could not be understood simply as another episode of communal tension between religious communities. It was deeply embedded in the history of colonial-era migration, the changing political geography of the Arakan region, competing narratives of belonging and the post-independence construction of citizenship in Myanmar. The historical relationship between the territories that now constitute Bangladesh and Myanmar, population movements during British colonial rule and the subsequent politicisation of identity were essential to understanding the dispute. The tendency to reduce the issue to a humanitarian concern or communal violence obscured these deeper historical and political dimensions.

articles.title: Draft of COP31 cover text drops references to fossil fuel phase-out, net zero dates
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A major concern raised by developing countries, of phasing out unilateral trade measures such as the CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) by 2027, that was present in the earlier draft has also been eliminated

The latest iteration of the COP 31 draft cover text has eliminated references to fossil fuel phase-out and net-zero dates but has also deleted references to a firm $120 billion adaptation-finance target that developing countries have been asking for as “legally binding financial obligations” on developed countries. This suggests that the most ambitious demands of both the developed and developing country blocs have been eliminated.

A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome it needs the consensus of all Parties. The Presidency has said earlier drafts were not meant to reflect consensus.

The COP31 Presidency’s revised draft cover decision, dated November 19, has 80 paragraphs, down from 144 in the November 16 version. The summit officially ends on November 20, though negotiations frequently overshoot into the weekend.

A major concern raised by developing countries, of phasing out unilateral trade measures such as the CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) by 2027, that was present in the earlier draft has also been eliminated.

However, a widely expected outcome of raising electricity’s share in final energy consumption to 35% by 2035, scaling up the use of carbon capture utilisation technologies and making early warning systems universal by 2027, continue to find mention in the text. A broad commitment to triple adaptation finance also remains.

“ The draft cover text weaves the 35% electricity in final energy consumption by 2035, alongside tripling renewable energy capacity and doubling the rate of energy efficiency improvement by 2030, ” Ajay Mathur, India’s lead negotiator at Paris COP and former DG, International Solar Alliance, said in a statement. The electricity use in India went up by 13% in 2025 due to the Hormuz crisis alone. It will be an ambitious goal for India to achieve 35% electrification by 2035, but due to the increasing amount of renewable energy in the Indian energy mix, we will be near the 32-34% mark by 2035. ”

“We’re down to the wire at COP31, and the latest texts are alarmingly far from ambitious or equitable,” said Rachel Cleetus, Climate Program director at the Union of Concerned Scientists (UCS) in a statement. “Rich nations, most notably the EU nations, are still holding a harsh line against committing to tripling adaptation finance to at least $120 billion annually by 2035. Instead of reaching agreement on urgently needed climate finance, some countries seem willing to push negotiations toward failure.”

articles.title: Talks without peace: On Russia, Ukraine, U.S. talks
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Europe must be part of any settlement on the Ukraine war

The trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. earlier this month failed to produce a major breakthrough or bridge the wide gap between Kyiv and Moscow. Yet, they were a good beginning towards finding a political settlement to Europe’s longest war since the Second World War . In the two-day talks, hosted by the U.S., the warring sides agreed on some humanitarian measures, including prisoner exchange. U.S. representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow after the talks to discuss the proposal. In the next stage, U.S., Ukrainian and European officials will meet in Berlin to discuss a coordinated European and Ukrainian position towards the peace process. As of now, Russian and Ukrainian positions remain far apart. Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the territories of Donbas it still controls to stop attacks. Russia also wants to introduce limits to Ukrainian military capabilities and Kyiv to declare neutrality (give up its NATO ambitions). Ukraine, on the other hand, has rejected making any territorial concessions for a settlement and asked for security guarantees from the West so that Russia would not attack the country again.

That Ukraine survived Russia’s invasion and continued to resist Russian forces for almost five years is no small feat. But it has also paid a huge price for its resistance. The country has lost more than 20% of its territory. Millions have fled, while men of fighting age are being drafted into the military . Ukraine’s economy is kept afloat by European support, while its military continues to rely on NATO for weapons and other supplies. Until recently, the West stood united in its support for Ukraine against Russia, but that unity has since begun to fray. U.S. President Donald Trump, who has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, is seeking to reset Washington’s ties with Moscow . European leaders, who initially sought to isolate Russia, have also started reestablishing contacts with the Kremlin. In October, Finnish and Norwegian leaders held direct talks with Mr. Putin. To be sure, Ukraine’s long-range strikes can hurt Russia, as the recent attack on the Kerch Bridge demonstrated. But such strikes are unlikely to change the Kremlin’s thinking about the war. As the conflict drags on, Ukraine’s position is weakening, and its allies are growing increasingly divided. After almost five years, Russia has failed to take a decisive victory. Ukraine does not have a credible path towards victory either. A diplomatic settlement, therefore, is the only way forward. The Abu Dhabi talks recognised this reality. But for the process to be meaningful, Europe must also be brought to the negotiating table.

articles.title: Agricultural workers’ body seeks lease payments, plots for assigned landowners in Amaravati
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nearly 1,800 acres of assigned land were taken over for the capital, mostly from Dalit and weaker sections, the union says

The Andhra Pradesh Agricultural Workers’ Union has demanded that the State government immediately pay annual lease amounts and allot residential and commercial plots to farmers who surrendered assigned lands for the construction of the capital at Amaravati.

In a statement on Friday, union State president D. Ramadevi and general secretary K. Lokanadham said nearly 1,800 acres of assigned land had been taken over in the Amaravati region for capital development. Most of the beneficiaries of these lands belonged to poor Dalit and weaker sections, they said.

The union leaders pointed out that the 2013 Land Acquisition Act provided for assigned landowners to receive the same rights and benefits as those holding patta lands, irrespective of whether the land was acquired through land pooling or compulsory acquisition. It alleged that the Central and State governments were violating the provisions of the law by denying assigned landowners their rightful entitlements.

The leaders said that when Amaravati was established in 2014, assigned landowners had also surrendered their lands along with other farmers, based on assurances that they would receive annual lease payments and residential and commercial plots on a par with owners of patta lands. However, these assurances had not been fulfilled so far, they alleged.

The landowners were facing severe livelihood difficulties as they had lost their agricultural land and had no alternative means of employment. The government had a responsibility to provide them relief at least by clearing the pending lease payments, the union leaders said.

They demanded that the government immediately release the lease amounts and allot residential and commercial plots to all eligible assigned landowners. Warning of an agitation, they said the union would be compelled to launch protests if the government failed to address their demands.

indian meteorological department said that Cyclonic Storm “Akvan” over the west-central Bay of Bengal crossed the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur.

articles.title: Supreme Court allows lighting of lamp on ‘Deepathoon’ at Thirupparankundram as limited one-time arrangement
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar however stayed the conclusive findings of the Madras HC in a January 6 judgment that upheld the right to light the lamp on the ‘Deepathoon’ as an essential practice

The Supreme Court on Friday (November 20, 2026) allowed the lighting of the lamp, as a “limited one-time arrangement”, on the ‘Deepathoon’ at the Thirupparankundram Hill on Karthigai Deepam day (November 24, 2026).

A Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar, however, stayed the conclusive findings of the Madras High Court in a January 6 judgment that upheld the right to light the lamp on the ‘Deepathoon’ as an essential practice.
The court issued notice on the appeals filed by the State.

The interim order dealt with pleas by the State to stay the January 6 judgment and also looked into the question whether the lamp could be lit on the ‘Deepathoon’ on the forthcoming Karthigai Deepam festival day falling on November 24.

Pronouncing the interim order, Justice Kumar said the court was aware of the dangers of allowing once becoming a precedent, while also noting that two separate Benches of the High Court had allowed the lighting of the lamp.
Imposing restrictions and safeguards, the Supreme Court directed that the Devasthanam would exclusively decide the members of the team to light the lamp on November 24.

The Madurai District Collector would act as nodal officer for the event. The Commissioner of Madurai Police has to provide the ring of security. The Centre was directed to supplement security arrangements with CRPF personnel, if required.
No procession, slogan-raising or permission to gathering of general public will be allowed, the court directed.
The access to lamp-lighting would be allowed to only authorised persons.
The team would immediately leave the spot of the ‘Deepathoon’ after lighting the lamp without leaving behind any temporary or permanent installation or objects, the court ordered

articles.title: Keralam to procure 25,000 tonnes of rice from FCI for market intervention in December
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Food and Civil Supplies Department has sanctioned the purchase at a cost of ₹59.75 crore, which will be met from the budgetary allocation under the relevant head for the 2026-27 financial year

The Keralam government will procure 25,000 metric tonnes of rice from the Food Corporation of India (FCI) under the Open Market Sale Scheme (OMSS) for distribution among ration card holders in December as part of its efforts to contain a possible increase in market prices.
The Food and Civil Supplies Department has sanctioned the purchase at a cost of ₹59.75 crore, which will be met from the budgetary allocation under the relevant head for the 2026-27 financial year.

Under the proposed distribution arrangement, non-priority ration card holders will receive five kg of either parboiled or raw rice per card, while priority category card holders will be given three kg of raw rice per card. The rice will be distributed at a subsidised rate of ₹27 a kg.

Official sources point out that the intervention is necessary in view of the possibility of an increase in rice prices and demand in the state’s open market, especially during the festive season in December. Increasing the availability of rice in the market through the public distribution system would help contain price increases and ensure price stability, they said.
The decision was taken on the basis of a detailed proposal submitted by the Commissioner of Civil Supplies.

articles.title: Madras High Court dismisses as withdrawn former Minister C. Vijayabaskar’s plea in gutkha case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: His counsel withdraws the plea with liberty to file a fresh case with a proper prayer after judges say two distinct prayers ought not to have been clubbed together

The Madras High Court on Friday (November 20, 2026) dismissed as withdrawn a case filed by former AIADMK Health Minister C. Vijayabaskar (now with the TVK) to quash a criminal case pending against him before a special court for Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) cases in Chennai in connection with the 2016 illegal gutkha and pan masala sale case.

The petitioner’s counsel withdrew the case after Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan said the litigant ought not to have clubbed two distinct reliefs: one challenging the constitutionality of certain entries under the provisions of the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003, and another seeking to quash the criminal case.

Justice Murugan told the counsel that the clubbing of two reliefs in one writ petition would only force the court to presume that the plea to quash the criminal prosecution had been camouflaged as a challenge to certain entries in the COTPA, 2003. He said it would be advisable for the petitioner to withdraw the present plea and file a fresh case with a proper prayer.

The counsel’s argument that both prayers were interconnected did not cut ice with the judges, who said that the petitioner ought to have confined his prayer to either of the two reliefs. “We cannot allow this camouflaging,” Justice Murugan said and pointed out that permitting such a course of action would set a wrong precedent. The Bench granted liberty to the petitioner to file a fresh case with a proper prayer.

The Income Tax Department had stumbled upon certain incriminating materials related to the illegal manufacture and sale of gutkha in Tamil Nadu and reported the issue to the Chief Secretary as well as the Director General of Police. In 2017, the then DMK MLA J. Anbazhagan (since dead) filed a writ petition in the High Court seeking an investigation by a Special Investigation Team (SIT).

The petitioner had insisted that the SIT be headed by a retired High Court judge and comprise officials drawn from the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). Disposing of the writ petition on April 26, 2018, the then Chief Justice Indira Banerjee (since retired) and Justice Abdul Quddhose had ordered a CBI probe into the issue, considering the harmful effects of consuming chewable tobacco such as gutkha.

“As trade in gutkha and other forms of chewable tobacco is spread over and/or passes through several States and there is a strong likelihood of involvement of high dignitaries and/or officials – both of the Central Government and the State Government and various others, we feel that the investigation should be carried out by a centralized agency,” the Bench had said.

articles.title: U.K., E.U to announce youth mobility deal, as they discuss closer ties
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The two sides are expected to announce a scheme for 100,000 18-32 year olds to live and work across each other’s borders

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham is expected to agree new terms for Britain’s relationship with the E.U. as he meets with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen in Brussels on November 20 at a Summit meeting. Mr Burnham has said in recent weeks that Brexit had caused “more harm than good”.

The two sides are expected to announce a scheme for 100,000 18-32 year olds to live and work across each other’s borders. In addition, they are working on closer ties in food and drink and linking the carbon trading schemes of the U.K. and the EU, as per reports.
“There’s the possibility of lower food prices, I can’t turn my back on that,” Mr Burnham said.
The summit is expected to announce the start of a dialogue on migration — including returns of irregular migrants to third countries.

The deal is a significant step to closer ties but is not expected to be the post-Brexit “reset” with Brussels that the Labour Party has sought . Mr Burnham, who is taking forward some of the discussions held with Brussels by his predecessor Keir Starmer, has committed to keeping to the red lines outlined in the Labour 2024 manifesto for the duration of this parliament (2029).

These red lines include not joining the bloc, nor its customs union and single market, and not allowing the “free movement” of people across UK-EU borders. However, Mr Burnham has said the U.K. would have to decide on its long-term options for its ties with the E.U. — including rejoining the E.U. The nature of the future relationship between the U.K. and E.U. is likely to be a campaign issue when Britain approaches its next general election.
“Business across the country have been clear, our current deal with the EU is not good enough,” said UK minister for EU relations, Hamish Falconer.

Mr Burnham had earlier said he would present legislation to the U.K. Parliament next week on this week’s agreements with Brussels. The U.K. will need harmonize some of its laws with the E.U.’s (i.e., follow them) to operationalize any deal on agriculture for instance.

articles.title: Asian American women feel impact of Nvidia CEO affair scandal, 'spy' accusations
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Asian American women working in tech, civil rights advocacy and academia have felt a sense of dread that this ordeal will diminish how their peers are viewed and treated in their workplaces. It’s a reminder that no accomplishments will completely dispel centuries-old stereotypes

The reveal earlier this month that billionaire Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had extramarital affairs sent shock waves through the tech world, particularly with Asian Americans who revered him as a once-in-a-generation talent.
But what has hit hard for Asian American women is the discourse around the allegation that Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman at the centre of the scandal, was possibly a spy.
Almost immediately, videos and memes reviving tired tropes fetishising Asian women hit social media.

“So few Asian women in general make it to the news for positive things. This is just going to continue to perpetuate negative stereotypes or biases for Asian women," said Misa Chien, founder of a network for Asian American women leaders called The Authentic Asian. Whether or not the allegation is true, “just the news will definitely influence people's opinions of women who have broken the ceiling or are trying to.”

Asian American women working in tech, civil rights advocacy and academia have felt a sense of dread that this ordeal will diminish how their peers are viewed and treated in their workplaces. It's a reminder that no accomplishments will completely dispel centuries-old stereotypes.
Jensen Huang has since resigned . However, the U.S. Justice Department has not found sufficient evidence that Alice Huang , who is not related to Jensen Huang, was a spy.
“I don't know if that's been determined yet," President Donald Trump told reporters this week.

Among the social media posts being spread was a collage of photos showing CEOs with Asian female partners. Author May-Lee Chai, who has written about the treatment of Asian women throughout history, called it “disgusting.”
Depicting them like trophy wives "implicates these spouses like they're somehow similar to this suspected spy,” said Ms. Chai, a creative writing professor at San Francisco State University.

The speed at which people glommed onto the Asian female spy narrative was shocking to April Moh, chief marketing officer for a financial technology company and board member of Stand with Asian Americans, a legal civil rights organisation specialising in combating workplace anti-Asian discrimination. The chatter has also led to women sharing stories of uncomfortable interactions.

articles.title: White House fires cybersecurity chief after widespread outages
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Sean Cairncross’ role will be filled in an acting capacity by current Defense Department Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies

Cyber security chief Sean Cairncross was fired from his post, a source close to the White House told AFP on Thursday (November 19, 2026), following major outages and growing concerns about AI threats.
U.S. President Donald Trump fully supported the firing because Mr. Cairncross lacked proper credentials to perform the job, the source said.

His role will be filled in an acting capacity by current Defense Department Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies, who has more appropriate credentials and has been Senate-confirmed, the source said.

In recent days and weeks, major outages in America have disrupted travel, communications and e-commerce for countless users, but also affected a top-secret internal communications network at the National Security Administration.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio congratulated Davies on X, writing: “Congratulations to the new National Cyber Director Kirsten Davies — look forward to working together to strengthen America’s cybersecurity.”
Prior to serving as National Cyber Director, Mr. Cairncross filled various roles as a White House insider during Trump’s first term.
Prior to that, MR. Cairncross worked as the Republican National Committee’s Chief Operating Officer for the 2016 election cycle.

fullParagraphs: USCIRF is a bipartisan body of ⁠the U.S. government that monitors religious freedom around the world and makes policy recommendations, which are not binding

India has escalated its targeting of religious minorities ‌during a voter list revision that struck off tens of millions ​of names nationwide, a U.S. panel on religious freedom said on ⁠Thursday (November 19, 2026).

“The Indian gov’t is targeting Muslim citizens by removing them from voter rolls, calling them ‘foreigners,’ and now illegally deporting them,” Asif Mahmood, the chair of the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom, ‌said in a statement.
India’s voter list revision removed 130 million names, roughly the population of Mexico, in the largest deletion of voters in the ‌country’s history.

Data shows the omissions disproportionately affect Muslims , India’s largest minority, who ‌have ⁠faced what rights groups describe as exclusionary policies and rising discrimination since Prime ⁠Minister Narendra Modi took power in 2014.
The Election Commission of India says it was removing duplicate, deceased, shifted and otherwise ineligible voters and that anyone excluded in error can pursue ​appeals.
The revision has become entangled with ‌a separate drive to identify and expel suspected illegal immigrants, even though removal from the rolls does not itself establish that someone is a foreigner.

“The Indian government’s expulsion of its own citizens based on their Muslim faith is a shocking ‌escalation of tactics that target religious minorities,” said Gene Mills, a commissioner ​on the U.S. panel.

USCIRF is a bipartisan body of ⁠the U.S. government that monitors religious freedom around the world and makes policy recommendations, which are not binding. Washington has not acted on its recent recommendations on India.

articles.title: Rohingya in Bangladesh welcome UN court’s genocide verdict but say they want to go home to Myanmar
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: “The Rohingya have their own distinct culture, their own language, their own land and everything else that defines an ethnic group,” said a Rohingya community leader

Hundreds of Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh sat in front of a big screen at their sprawling camp in Cox’s Bazar, watching the news from the Netherlands, where the U.N.'s top court ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority in a brutal 2017 military operation.

For many, the historic verdict on Thursday (November 19, 2026) represented a “small victory” — offering a glimmer of hope that someday they would be able to return safely to their homes in Myanmar, across the border from Bangladesh.
It was a landmark judgement, finding Myanmar responsible for the crime against the country’s ethnic Rohingya — the first time the court ruled that a state committed genocide.

A Rohingya refugee gives a thumbs up while another person holds a placard following the announcement of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) verdict, in a case accusing Myanmar of committing genocide against the minority Rohingya population, at a refugee camp in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, November 19, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters

The Hague-based International Court of Justice also ordered Myanmar’s military-supported government to allow the Rohingya to return home safely, pay reparations to the Rohingya Muslims and prosecute those suspected of having committed genocide.

But it remains to be seen how much of the ruling can be implemented. The court’s rulings are final and legally binding, but it has no way to enforce them beyond reporting noncompliance to the U.N. Security Council.
There was no immediate reaction to the ruling from the Myanmar delegation in The Hague or from the government in Myanmar.
At the refugee camp in Cox’s Bazar, Rohingya refugees told The Associated Press of their concerns.

Mohammad Rofik, a Rohingya community leader at the camp, said the verdict was “a victory” for them as it recognised the genocide and the sufferings of their minority in the Buddhist-majority nation, but that it was “not an end” to their ordeal.
“Justice has started,” Mr. Rofik said, adding that the Rohingya still have “a long way to go.”

fullParagraphs: GPS-enabled collar helps forest officials track the movement; no attacks on cattle or human habitations reported so far

The tiger ‘Explorer’, which has been roaming across the Eastern Ghats after travelling through several States, has entered the Mylavaram forest range in the Vijayawada forest division and was seen in the A. Konduru forest block on Friday (November 20, 2026), triggering a fresh alert among forest officials.

The tiger is staying in a hilly stretch with thick forest cover and dense bush growth. Forest officials are tracking its movements with the help of a GPS-enabled satellite radio collar fitted to it following its capture and subsequent release into the Papikondalu National Park earlier this year. Officials said the tiger had not entered any human habitation so far and no cattle deaths or attacks on livestock had been reported in the Mylavaram range.
The villages of A. Konduru, Cheemalapadu, Vinagadapa and Narkulapadu, located in the vicinity of the forest block, have been alerted as a precautionary measure.

Forest personnel are monitoring the animal's movements and keeping a safe distance to avoid disturbing it. Officials said its movement was being tracked continuously, though its next direction of travel could not be predicted.

The tiger was first noticed in the Nuzvidu range a couple of days ago and moved towards the Mylavaram range overnight. It has been staying in the A. Konduru forest block since the following morning. Officials said it could move back towards Nuzvidu or proceed towards other forest stretches, depending on its movement.

A five-member specialised tiger conservation team from Pune, which had assisted the Forest Department during earlier operations, is involved in monitoring the animal. The team is equipped to tranquilise and capture the tiger if the situation warrants it.
Forest Department personnel are also using GPS equipment, drones and camera traps to keep track of its movements.
