articles.title: India’s smartphone sale plunged 22% during festive season
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The decline was much steeper than the pre-festive forecast of 12%. Market value, however, stayed broadly flat YoY, as ASPs grew 28% YoY, largely offsetting the fall in unit sales

As rising memory costs have been pushing smartphone prices to a new height, the impact of it was quite visible during the just concluded Indian festive season (October 8–November 10) which collapsed by an estimated 22% year-over-year (YoY), noted Counterpoint. The rising phone prices pushed a weaker demand as buyers held back their purchases.

“The decline was much steeper than the pre-festive forecast of 12%. Market value, however, stayed broadly flat YoY, as ASPs grew 28% YoY, largely offsetting the fall in unit sales,” the findings said.

The research firm highlighted that festive discounts narrowed to 10–25%, from 35–40% in 2025. “Even discounted entry-level models were generally priced higher than a year ago, putting upgrades out of reach for many price-sensitive buyers. Brands instead leaned on no-cost EMIs, bank offers and trade-ins, with 48% of smartphone sales being finance-led.”

During the first wave (October 8–18), volumes fell 19% YoY, with online sales falling short of the performance seen during earlier sale events. Online sales, which account for a significant share of smartphone purchases, declined as higher consumer traffic failed to translate into actual conversions.

During festive season also, Samsung had the best of lot with a 21% share, overtaking Vivo, as its sales fell 8% YoY against a 22% market decline. Galaxy S25 Ultra and Galaxy S25 drew strong demand, while Samsung delayed price hikes until after the sales and managed inventory better than rivals.
Vivo and Oppo declined 21% and 24%, respectively, holding up better in mainline retail through retailer incentives and bundled offers, but were weaker online.

Apple’s sales declined by double digits YoY despite strong feedback for the new iPhone 18 Pro series and continued consumer interest in the iPhone 17. However, refurbished iPhones saw strong demand as consumers sought more affordable options, which hurt demand for new iPhones.
Xiaomi declined sharply, though its sales picked up around Diwali, driven by the Redmi Note 15 and Note 17 series.
Google was the fastest growing brand in the ultra-premium segment (45,000+) as Google sold its highest ever pixel devices during festive season.
Brands with exposure to the sub-20,000 segment were hit hardest, declining by close to 50%.

articles.title: The hidden cost of handing a smartphone to a child | Explained
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Paediatricians are witnessing an alarming trend: smartphones being increasingly used as “digital pacifiers” to appease toddlers during mealtime, soothe them when they throw a tantrum and keeping them engaged while managing household chores

As toddlers swiping through smartphone screens before holding a pencil has become a common sight, paediatricians are worried about an alarming trend: smartphones being increasingly used as “digital pacifiers” to appease toddlers during mealtime, soothe them when they throw a tantrum and keep them engaged while managing household chores. This phenomenon is no longer confined to urban households.

A study conducted by AIIMS Delhi, and published in the Indian Journal of Medical Research in April 2026, surveyed 282 children aged 2 to 4 years in rural Haryana. Its findings revealed that half of all the children surveyed exceeded the World Health Organisation’s (WHO) recommended screen time limit of an hour per day for children between 2 to 4 years. The research underlines a pervasive reliance on smartphones to keep children engaged, across all socio-economic layers.

As toddlers swiping through smartphone screens before holding a pencil has become a common sight, paediatricians are worried about an alarming trend: smartphones being increasingly used as “digital pacifiers” to appease toddlers during mealtime, soothe them when they throw a tantrum and keep them engaged while managing household chores. The research underlines a pervasive reliance on smartphones to keep children engaged, across all socio-economic layers.

articles.title: Rare ‘bridal veil’ bamboo mushroom spotted near Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A biologist stumbled upon the elusive and short-lived bamboo mushroom in Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary earlier this week.

S. Gagana, biologist and nature education officer at Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary in Srirangapatna, described the sighting amidst the woodland floor of the bird sanctuary on November 17 as a “delightful encounter.”

“With its dark cap, white stalk and delicate lace-like skirt, the mushroom looked like a tiny bridal veil amidst the forest floor. It was indeed a fortunate moment to witness this fascinating fungus in its natural habitat,” she said.
Scientifically known as Phallus indusiatus, the bamboo mushroom, popularly referred to as “veiled lady” or bamboo pith, derives its common name from its close association with bamboo thickets.

“However, it can also grow in other moist, shaded habitats rich in decaying leaves and organic matter. The net-like structure surrounding its stalk is called an indusium, which gives it the distinctive appearance of a veil,” Gagana explained.

Deputy Conservator of Forests (Mysuru Wildlife Division) Prabhu Gowda noted that the fungus grows on deadwood bamboo when moisture and temperature conditions are favourable, adding that it also emits a distinctive odour.

Interestingly, the bamboo mushroom is considered a delicacy in several Asian cuisines and is used in soups and stir-fries after proper processing. However, Gagana cautioned that wild mushrooms should never be consumed without expert identification.

C. Hemavathi, retired professor of Botany at Government First Grade College in Mysuru, confirmed the species identity, noting that while the fungus is not uncommon in wetter regions like Kodagu, its emergence in Ranganathittu’s riverine habitat is noteworthy.
“The sighting reminds us that Ranganathittu’s biodiversity extends well beyond its avian visitors, and even the forest floor holds fascinating wonders waiting to be discovered,” Ms. Gagana said.

The Smart 4 Pro sports a 13MP rear camera and a 5MP front camera.
Lava Smart 4 Pro has been priced at ₹10,999. It will be available in Neelam Blue and Konark Gold colours.

articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Tugan-Baranovsky argued that machines can produce machines which can produce more machines, while Luxemburg contended that machines are not an end in themselves; only time will tell who is right

Building on our previous piece yesterday, we now look at the macroeconomic implications of rising labour productivity on the global economy. We make the global economy our canvas to avoid between-country gain/loss that AI may result in since that is not the purpose of this piece. Our basic question is what may happen to the global pie of output and jobs. When looked at globally, demand consists of consumption, investment, and government expenditure because the trade component cancels out. (Refer Infobox below)

Since government intervention is outside the sphere of “pure” market economy, we focus on consumption and investment. The question we pose in this piece is how a rise in productivity would affect this demand? By its very nature, this piece is speculative, so we present two opposite cases for the readers to mull over.

A rise in labour productivity, without a commensurate increase in real wages, means a fall in the share of wages (denominator of the last term rises but the numerator does not rise in tandem in Infobox below). The implication of this is significant for consumption growth.

Let us say the total output of 100 is divided equally between workers and capitalists and, for the sake of the argument, workers consume all their wages and capitalists consume half of it. The total consumption demand would be 75; 50 by the workers and 25 (half of 50) by the capitalists. Suppose AI is introduced in this economy which increases workers’ productivity dramatically but the wages rise by less than that, so the wage share falls to, say 30%. The consumption demand of the workers fall to 30, whereas for the capitalists it rises to 35 (half of 70), totalling to 65. Demand for consumption falls from 75 to 65, so demand worth 10 just disappears into thin air.

More than a century ago, a theoretical debate took place between Rosa Luxemburg, a German Marxist, and Mikhail Tugan-Baranovsky, a Russian economist on the issue of falling share of consumption in total demand and growth in a capitalist economy. It would be apt to revisit that debate in the context of AI and rising labour productivity.

Tugan-Baranovsky argued that even if the share of consumption falls, investment can replace the lost demand. The 10 units of consumption goods that vanished into thin air above could simply get replaced by investment demand. He went to the extreme to argue that machines can produce machines which can produce more machines even if the demand for the final consumption goods they produce shrinks over time. The case of AI, imagined as machines producing more machines, comes very close to what he had in mind.

Luxemburg argued, on the other hand, that machines are not an end in themselves. If the demand for the final consumption goods they produce is decreasing over time, there will be a surplus of such goods piling in the warehouses. The 10 units of consumption not sold will not be produced next time. And if they are not produced, then the machines which could produce them will lie idle. This would dissuade the capitalists from making more machines. Let alone machines producing more machines for the sake of it, there will be a contraction of investment in machines.

The implication of her argument is clear. Of the two sources of demand, investment is unique. It creates both the capacity to produce output (say a factory which produces motorcycles) and the demand for output (construction of the motorcycle factory gives rise to demand for goods like cement, steel etc. which goes into building the factory). Looking at the level of the economy, if the capacity to produce output expands faster than the demand for it, there will be a contraction of investment eventually.

To be sure, there are other possibilities. None of this may happen if one of the following conditions holds. One, while productivity rises in the sector affected by AI, it may give rise to demand in sectors where labour productivity is quite low. Seen at the macro level, total labour productivity, which is the average of high labour productivity in AI sectors and lower productivity in the rest of the economy, may remain the same as it was in the pre-AI age. Two, even if overall labour productivity rises, wages rise in proportion, in which case the very source of a fall in the wage share disappears. This seems unlikely under capitalism though. Three, even if the wage share falls, investment demand could replace the lost consumption demand because AI requires more intensive capital investment to cater to the final demand.

Even though it is difficult to isolate specifically which component of investment is exclusively associated with AI, there is a broad consensus in the literature that the bulk of it would show up under the category computers and peripherals. The Chart below shows that investment in AI seems to be off the charts compared to any other component of investment. For comparison with other components of investment and GDP, we have created an index which starts at 100 in 2021 for all the variables under consideration. While nominal GDP has risen 1.5 times, investment in AI has risen 3.5 times within a short span of less than two years.

articles.title: Workshop on Alumni-Academia-Industry Partnership to mark Mining Education’s golden jubilee in Kothagudem
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Alumni of Mining Engineers’ Association (Osmania and Kakatiya Universities), Kothagudem, is organising a one-day workshop on “Alumni-Academia-Industry Partnership” on November 21, 2026, to mark the Golden Jubilee of Mining Education at Kothagudem.

The workshop is being organised in association with the Mining Engineers’ Association of India, Singareni Chapter, according to a press release. The event will bring together academic and industry perspectives to explore ways for bridging the gap between academic learning and industry requirements, while promoting innovation, skill development, research and entrepreneurship.
It will also deliberate on collaborative initiatives to enhance the quality of education and improve students’ employability.
Minister for Agriculture Tummala Nageswara Rao will be the chief guest, while Kothagudem MLA K. Sambasiva Rao will be the guest of honour at the inaugural session.

The technical sessions will be followed by the Golden Jubilee celebrations at the Open-Air Theatre of Dr. Manmohan Singh Earth Sciences University of Telangana, Kothagudem, at 2.30 p.m. on the same day.

articles.title: YC, SFI complain against police personnel over photos with accused
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Youth Congress and the Students Federation of India (SFI) have lodged separate complaints alleging that police officers were photographed with persons accused in serious criminal cases. The complaints were submitted to Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala and the Director General of Police (DGP).

Youth Congress Kannur district president Vijil Mohanan filed a complaint against Jayesh, an officer attached to the Sreekandapuram police station, after a photograph purportedly showing the officer with the accused in a case involving an attack on a Sreekandapuram municipality councillor was circulated.

The Youth Congress alleged that Jayesh had intervened to prevent the arrest of the accused until they secured anticipatory bail. Speaking to the media, Mr. Mohanan called for an inquiry and action against the officer over his alleged association with the accused. Jayesh is a former district office-bearer of the police association. Meanwhile, the SFI Kannur district committee approached the DGP seeking disciplinary action against two Kannur City police personnel for allegedly posing for photographs with Athul M.C., one of the accused in a case involving an alleged attempt to murder students of Nirmalagiri College, Koothuparamba, on September 4, 2026.

In his complaint, SFI Kannur district committee secretary Joyal Thomas identified the personnel as civil police officers C. Nijin and Suresh Narikkottan, both attached to the Kannur City police district headquarters. The complaint stated that the photographs were subsequently circulated in various groups.

Mr. Thomas said that maintaining friendly relations with people accused in serious criminal cases and circulating such photographs could undermine the dignity and impartiality of the police. He alleged that the conduct violated the Kerala Police Act, the Kerala Government Servants’ Conduct Rules and social media guidelines.

He said such conduct could affect investigations, weaken public confidence in the justice system and embolden accused persons. He called for a departmental inquiry and strict action against the officers for alleged dereliction of duty and indiscipline.

articles.title: Working class in India is mobilising and resisting attack from many fronts: World Federation of Trade Unions leader
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Pambis Kyritsis is in Bengaluru to participate in the two-day Asia Pacific region conference of the WFTU that commenced here from Friday

The general secretary of the World Federation of Trade Unions (WFTU), Pambis Kyritsis, on Friday said that the working class in India is mobilising and resisting the attack from the neoliberal government and capitalists from both within and outside the country that are shrinking their rights to promote work without protection.

“The attack is from the neoliberal government, the four labour codes and capitalists of this country and outside to shrink rights and deny any collective bargaining and collective agreement. But what is encouraging is that we see a very effective alliance among working labour movement and agriculture,” he told presspersons here.

Mr. Kyritsis is in Bengaluru to participate in the two-day Asia Pacific region conference of the WFTU that commenced here from Friday. Founded in 1945, post the World War II, the WFTU is present in more than 130 countries. In India, seven central trade unions are its affiliates. It represents more than 110 million workers all over the world and, through its seven affiliates, represents more than 20 million workers.

Kyritsis said that the conference was taking place at a time when workers around the world are facing challenges of many kinds. He cited “the genocide of the Palestinian people in Gaza, the attacks against the population in the West Bank by the Israel Army and settlers, supported and encouraged by the United States, the European Union, and their allies, the attacks on Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, the crude attempt to strangle Cuba through illegal and immoral economic energy blockade, the intervention in Venezuela and the abduction of the country’s president.” More workers through their trade unions are resisting and refusing to work for the war, to work for the war economy, he added.

Stating that Asia Pacific region is increasingly becoming a key focus of imperialist interests, he said, “The only encouraging and hopeful element within this depressing picture is that workers are not possibly accepting this anti-people and anti-worker attacks. Guided by class-oriented trade unions, millions of workers around the world are choosing the path of struggle, to defend their trade, union, social and political rights. Through million mobilisations, in every corner of the globe, they demand jobs with rights that ensure the satisfaction of their contemporary needs.”

The union leader felt that the cost of living crisis — currently unfolding in Europe — is a universal phenomenon and not of one country or continent, and that increasing of prices is hurting much more the poor people. He also said that once the workers agitate at one place, it will have triggering effect on others in a global village when the impact is felt immediately elsewhere.

articles.title: Supreme Court allows lighting of lamp on deepathoon at Thirupparankundram as limited one-time arrangement
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar, however, stayed the conclusive findings of the Madras High Court in a January 6 judgment that upheld the right to light the lamp on the deepathoon as an essential practice

The Supreme Court on Friday (November 20, 2026) allowed the lighting of the lamp, as a “limited one-time arrangement”, on the deepathoon at the Thirupparankundram Hill in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai district on Karthigai Deepam day (November 24).

A Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar, however, stayed the conclusive findings of the Madras High Court in a January 6 judgment that upheld the right to light the lamp on the deepathoon as an essential practice. The court issued notice on the appeals filed by the State.
The interim order dealt with pleas by the State to stay the January 6 judgment and looked into the question whether the lamp could be lit on the deepathoon on the coming Karthigai Deepam day.

The deepathoon (stone lamp pillar) is around 50 metres from the Sikandar Badusha Dargah. While the dargah is at the hilltop, the Subramaniya Swamy Temple is at the base of the hillock. The court’s interim arrangement comes amid a dispute between Hindu worshippers and the dargah on the ownership of the hilltop and the deepathoon site

“What weighs with us at this stage is the peculiar nature of the occasion and the proximity of the festival, which is scheduled to take place on November 24. The opportunity to perform the ceremony on that particular day, if denied, cannot be restored by any subsequent adjudication. Equally, we are conscious that the performance of the ceremony, once permitted, cannot be undone,” said the order.

The Bench, comprising Justice P.B. Varale, said there was a need to balance the immediacy of the festival with the need to ensure that the interim order would not prejudice the appeal of the State or become fodder for claims of a vested right. “We are of the view that a limited, one-time arrangement, subject to stringent safeguards, would appropriately balance the interests involved pending further consideration,” the court observed.

Imposing a series of restrictions and safeguards, the court directed that the Subramaniya Swamy Temple Devasthanam would exclusively decide the members of the team to light the lamp on November 24. It ordered that the composition and number of the team would be settled by the Madurai Collector in consultation with the temple’s Executive Officer, the Archaeological Survey of India, and the Commissioner of Police, Madurai. The Collector would act as the nodal officer for the event. The Commissioner of the Madurai City Police has to provide the ring of security. The Centre was directed to supplement security arrangements with CRPF personnel, if required.
The Bench banned any kind of procession, public congregation, demonstration, slogan-raising or activity extraneous to the ceremonial lighting of the lamp at the site.

The leeway given for November 24 should not be construed as a judicial recognition of an essential religious practice, the court emphasised repeatedly. “We make it abundantly clear that the present arrangement does not proceed upon any finding that the stone pillar is, or has historically been, a place of customary religious observance. Nor does it determine whether the lighting of the lamp at the location constitutes an essential religious practice or whether any individual, religious denomination or institution possesses an enforceable right in that regard. All questions concerning title, possession, customary usage, religious entitlement, temple administration, and access to the site are expressly left open,” the court underscored.

The access to lamp-lighting would be allowed to only authorised persons. The team would immediately leave the spot of the ‘deepathoon’ after lighting the lamp without leaving behind any temporary or permanent installation or objects, the court ordered. No damage or change would be made to any religious monument, including the nearby dargah on the Hill, the interim order stated, adding that the access and enjoyment of worshippers to the dargah should not be disturbed.

articles.title: Messi visit row: Keralam govt. grants sanction to investigate former Sports Minister V. Abdurahiman
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to an order issued by the Home department, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the case has been cleared to incorporate relevant sections of the Prevention of Corruption Act into its ongoing investigation

The State government on Friday issued orders to accord sanction under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, to investigate former Minister for Sports, Minority Welfare and Waqf, V. Abdurahiman, along with two other former officials, over the alleged financial and procedural irregularities linked to the aborted visit of the Argentina national football team to the State.

According to an order issued by the Home department, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the case has been cleared to incorporate relevant sections of the Prevention of Corruption Act into its ongoing investigation.

Alongside Mr. Abdurahiman, who has been named as the third accused in the case, the government has sanctioned probes against his former private secretary C. Sathyapalan, and former Kerala State Sports Council president U. Sharafali, who are the fourth and fifth accused respectively.

The order follows a formal request from the State Police Chief based on a preliminary report submitted by the SIT. The government observed that an independent perusal of the SIT’s findings disclosed a prima facie case warranting an investigation into recommendations made and decisions taken by the former Minister and the officials during their tenure. The government had earlier received sanction from the Keralam Lok Bhavan to prosecute the former Minister.

The SIT is headed by Additional Director General of Police (Law and Order) P. Vijayan. The investigation centres on the high-profile bid by the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) administration to host World Cup winners Argentina, led by Lionel Messi, for an international friendly match in Keralam.

Following the the United Democratic Front’s (UDF) into power six months ago, the Sports Department flagged severe administrative lapses and financial discrepancies in the arrangements for the proposed visit, thereby prompting the investigation.

The SIT had earlier registered a case against event sponsor Reporter Broadcasting Company (RBC) and its managing director, Anto Augustine, who are listed as the first and second accused, respectively. The investigators have alleged that the former Minister and his aides bypassed standard departmental procedures and tender norms to extend undue financial benefits to the private broadcaster.

fullParagraphs: The 16th round of commercial mine auctions put forth 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.
The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions has attracted 83 bids for 17 coal blocks with 20 first-time bidders seeking to enter commercial coal mining, signalling fresh interest in the sector.
The Union Coal Ministry said on Friday that 17 blocks offered in the latest round received 83 bids. In addition, the second attempt to auction one coal block from the 15th round attracted two bids.
Taking the 26 blocks covered by the auction process into account, the number of bids has quadrupled compared with the previous round, the ministry said.
The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions was launched on September 17, offering 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.

“Competition in the current round has been intense, with 16 of the 26 blocks attracting multiple bids. The round has also brought 20 first-time bidders into the commercial coal mining regime, a clear sign that the sector continues to draw new capital and new players,” the ministry said in a statement.

Since the introduction of the commercial coal mining auction regime in June 2020, the government has auctioned 145 coal mines across 15 rounds. These mines are estimated to generate annual revenues of around ₹47,500 crore, according to government estimates.

articles.title: CEA flags need to align capital markets with India’s development priorities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Equity market capitalisation stood at around 130% of GDP, while the corporate bond market accounted for only about 16%.

Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran has called for a greater role for Indian capital markets in channelising household savings into productive investments, stressing the importance of patient capital in meeting the country’s long-term development needs.

Speaking at the CII Financial Summit in Mumbai, Mr. Nageswaran said sectors such as infrastructure, manufacturing, agriculture and mineral exploration required long-term financing, given their extended investment horizons.
Highlighting the imbalance in India’s financial markets, he pointed out that equity market capitalisation stood at around 130% of GDP, while the corporate bond market accounted for only about 16%.

While acknowledging that technology had improved market access, settlement systems and transaction security, he said these advances had not necessarily translated into better outcomes for investors or the real economy.

“A safer machine is not the same as a better outcome,” he said, emphasising that technological innovation should ultimately strengthen the capital market’s core function of converting savings into productive investments.
Cautioning against a consumption-led economic model, Mr. Nageswaran said, “An economy that is consumption-oriented may not be the most suited one for India’s development context.”

Echoing the need to promote long-term savings, Gaurav Mathur, founder and managing director of SafeGold, called for tax incentives to encourage investors to hold financial assets for longer periods. He stressed that savings policies should reflect individuals’ financial circumstances and different stages of life.

“It’s a matter of constructive partnership between regulators and financial intermediaries, where you incentivise long-term saving behaviour at the appropriate stages in life,” Mr. Mathur said, adding that incentives should particularly target wealthier individuals with greater capacity to save.

Meanwhile, Nilesh Shah, managing director of Kotak Mahindra Asset Management Company and part-time member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, underscored the need to strengthen financial literacy and encourage voluntary pension savings. He said these measures were increasingly important amid uncertainties over employment and income in a technology-driven economy.

articles.title: How AI could reshape global growth and productivity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: A key expected impact of AI is an unprecedented rise in labour productivity, as its success as a technological revolution is premised on such an increase; what remains to be seen is how pervasive its impact will be across different sectors of the economy

Many have likened the artificial intelligence (AI) phenomenon to the inventions of the steam engine or internal combustion engine in the 18th and 19th centuries, respectively. Only time can tell whether AI is epochal of that kind. In this two-part piece, we discuss the possible impact it may have on the global economy as a whole.

A key impact of AI is considered to be an unprecedented rise in labour productivity. In fact, if there is one purpose AI is supposed to serve, it is enhancing labour productivity multifold. Since labour productivity is a key variable in this puzzle, consider what it constitutes of (Box 1) . It is a ratio of output and workers employed. Now this ratio can rise in three different ways — a rise in output for a given number of workers employed (rise in the numerator); a loss of jobs which leads to a fall in the denominator; more jobs are created, but the output rises faster than the jobs (while both the numerator and the denominator are rising, the numerator rises faster than the denominator).

There is usually a distinction drawn between a case where there is a net loss of jobs versus one where jobs grow, but the output grows even faster. The latter is preferred over the former. Even though AI may displace white-collar workers, it may generate more jobs for the blue-collar workers, so in the net there may not be a job loss with AI adoption across the economy. However, for the argument we make below, it does not matter which of the three sources leads to a rise in productivity. Why should the rise in labour productivity matter? There are two contrasting takes on this question in the economics discipline.

One which argues that productivity growth increases the growth of output in the economy. The idea is simple. Growth of output is a function of its two inputs — labour and capital. Since capital enhances the productivity of labour, the rate at which output can grow is the sum of the growth of the labour force and its productivity. So, if the workforce grows at 2% and productivity at 4%, the economy would stabilise at 6% growth over time. And if the rate of labour productivity rises, according to this framework, growth in the economy rises pari passu (Graph 1a).

Between the three variables — output growth, labour growth and productivity growth — output growth adjusts to the other two. This is what Robert Solow, a celebrated economist and a Nobel laureate, showed in a seminal paper on growth theory. 📈 Economic, Banking & Finance 📅 20 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 How AI could reshape global growth and productivity

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

A key expected impact of AI is an unprecedented rise in labour productivity, as its success as a technological revolution is premised on such an increase; what remains to be seen is how pervasive its impact will be across different sectors of the economy

Many have likened the artificial intelligence (AI) phenomenon to the inventions of the steam engine or internal combustion engine in the 18th and 19th centuries, respectively. Only time can tell whether AI is epochal of that kind. In this two-part piece, we discuss the possible impact it may have on the global economy as a whole.

A key impact of AI is considered to be an unprecedented rise in labour productivity. In fact, if there is one purpose AI is supposed to serve, it is enhancing labour productivity multifold. Since labour productivity is a key variable in this puzzle, consider what it constitutes of (Box 1) . It is a ratio of output and workers employed. Now this ratio can rise in three different ways — a rise in output for a given number of workers employed (rise in the numerator); a loss of jobs which leads to a fall in the denominator; more jobs are created, but the output rises faster than the jobs (while both the numerator and the denominator are rising, the numerator rises faster than the denominator).

There is usually a distinction drawn between a case where there is a net loss of jobs versus one where jobs grow, but the output grows even faster. The latter is preferred over the former. Even though AI may displace white-collar workers, it may generate more jobs for the blue-collar workers, so in the net there may not be a job loss with AI adoption across the economy. However, for the argument we make below, it does not matter which of the three sources leads to a rise in productivity. Why should the rise in labour productivity matter? There are two contrasting takes on this question in the economics discipline.

One which argues that productivity growth increases the growth of output in the economy. The idea is simple. Growth of output is a function of its two inputs — labour and capital. Since capital enhances the productivity of labour, the rate at which output can grow is the sum of the growth of the labour force and its productivity. So, if the workforce grows at 2% and productivity at 4%, the economy would stabilise at 6% growth over time. And if the rate of labour productivity rises, according to this framework, growth in the economy rises pari passu (Graph 1a).

Between the three variables — output growth, labour growth and productivity growth — output growth adjusts to the other two. This is what Robert Solow, a celebrated economist and a Nobel laureate, showed in a seminal paper on growth theory. What he did not explain though was why and where did this labour productivity rise come from. Much later, his successors argued that the growth of labour productivity depends on investment in human capital, research and development, patent regimes, etc., what came to be known as endogenous growth theories.

articles.title: Estonia to close border with Russia, Moscow decries 'new Iron Curtain'
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: NATO and EU member ‌Estonia on November 15 accused Russian security services of staging an attempted ‌arson ⁠attack on an Estonian defence company, in what it said ⁠was the second such incident this year

Estonia will close its road border crossings with Russia on security grounds for at least six months, the Baltic country's government ‌said on Friday (November 20, 2026), prompting a warning from Moscow that it would respond with political and diplomatic measures.

NATO and EU member ‌Estonia on Sunday (November 15, 2026) accused Russian security services of staging an attempted ‌arson ⁠attack on an Estonian defence company, in what it said ⁠was the second such incident this year.
This would help address the wider security situation and limit Russia's ability to ​organise further attacks, Estonian Interior Minister ‌Igor Taro told a press conference.
"Russian security services are intimidating and trying to recruit our citizens who are travelling through our border checkpoints. This is something we cannot tolerate anymore," Mr. Taro said.
The Kremlin has ‌denied any involvement in the weekend arson attack.
Foreign Ministry spokeswoman ​Maria Zakharova on Friday (November 20, 2026) said that Russia would respond with political and diplomatic measures if Estonia went ahead with the ⁠closure.
"Such moves are tantamount to attempts to erect a new Iron Curtain under the false pretence of some sort of threat from the East," ‌Ms. Zakharova said.
Estonia, a strong supporter of Ukraine, currently has five crossing points where travellers can enter or leave Russia, according to the government.
Estonia's northern neighbour Finland shut its Russia border crossings in 2023, and has kept them closed since then, while southern Baltic nations Latvia and Lithuania maintain open crossings.

Thousands of people living in Estonia have family in ‌Russia or vice versa, as legacies of the Soviet era. The crossing at Narva, a ​majority Russian-speaking city on the Estonian side of the border, is also used by people travelling from further afield in ⁠Europe to reach St. Petersburg a few hours' drive away.

articles.title: Pakistan Army chief Munir vows to eliminate terrorism from country
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Pakistan overall witnessed a significant decline in terrorism-related violence during October, with attacks falling by 37%, deaths resulting from these attacks declining by 57%, and injuries decreasing by 71% compared to September, said Dawn newspaper report

Pakistan’s Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir on Friday (November 20, 2026) expressed the “unwavering resolve” of the security forces to eliminate terrorism from the country during a visit to the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.
Mr. Munir, who is also the Chief of Defence Forces (CDF), said this during a visit to Miranshah in North Waziristan district, the military's media wing said in a statement.

“He reaffirmed the unwavering resolve of the security forces, in close coordination with law enforcement agencies, to decisively eliminate the menace of terrorism and preserve the hard-earned peace and stability of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa,” the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement.
Mr. Munir also appreciated the KP police and expressed pride in its resilience and sacrifices against terrorism and Fitna-al-Khawarij.
The term Fitna-al-Khawarij is used by the federal government for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

During the visit, the CDF was given a comprehensive briefing on “the prevailing security situation, ongoing intelligence-based operations [IBO] and measures being undertaken to consolidate the gains achieved through sustained counter-terrorism efforts, “ the ISPR statement said.
It added that CDF Munir also interacted with officers and troops and appreciated their “high level of preparedness, professionalism and unwavering commitment".
Security forces continue to carry out counterterrorism action in KP and Balochistan, the two provinces that have been particularly affected by terrorism in Pakistan.
On Saturday (November 14, 2026), ISPR said four troops, including a major, were killed while 24 terrorists were killed in IBOs in Balochistan and KP’s North Waziristan.
Furthermore, last week, 74 terrorists were killed in IBOs in KP and Balochistan.

articles.title: U.S. sanctions Myanmar armed group leader over scam links
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Treasury Department said on November 19 it had imposed an asset freeze on General Saw Shwe Wah, commander-in-chief of the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA), and one of his top officers, and had banned Americans from dealing with them
The United States has frozen the assets of the leader of an ethnic armed group in Myanmar and one of his lieutenants, accusing them of facilitating cyberscammers who target Americans.

Organised criminal gangs have, for years, carried out fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes from compounds in Southeast Asian nations, defrauding victims around the world of tens of billions of dollars annually.
The industry is adapting its operations in the wake of much-publicised crackdowns in Myanmar and Cambodia following Chinese pressure, often dissipating into smaller facilities in new locations.

The U.S. Treasury Department said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) it had imposed an asset freeze on General Saw Shwe Wah, commander-in-chief of the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA), and one of his top officers, and had banned Americans from dealing with them.
The DKBA is one of the myriad armed groups operating in Myanmar's borderlands, some of which have been fighting the government for decades.
It has signed a ceasefire with Yangon and is accused by the United States, which earlier sanctioned the organisation, of supporting scam centres.

"DKBA actors not only provide security for scam compounds and permit their continued operation, but also actively participate in violence against victims of human trafficking trapped inside the compounds," the U.S. Treasury said.
The DKBA's Colonel Saw A One, responsible for security in the Three Pagodas Pass area in Karen State near the Thai border, was also designated by the U.S. on Thursday (November 19, 2026).
Jason Tower, senior expert at the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime, told that last week the Three Pagodas Pass region has been a "major expansion area" for scam compounds.
The latest U.S. Treasury measures also sanctioned Zhao Hui, a China-born, naturalised Cambodian accused of running cyberscam compounds in Cambodia, and two of his companies.

articles.title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah to visit India on November 22-23
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: In his first India visit, Nepal Prime Minister is expected to sign several MoUs and inaugurate projects
Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will visit India on November 22-23, the Ministry of External Affairs announced on Friday (November 20, 2026).
Briefing the media in Kathmandu, Nepal’s Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai said Mr. Shah will be accompanied by a 34-member delegation.

#WATCH | Kathmandu | "On the invitation of the Prime Minister of India, Nepali PM Balendra Shah will embark on a State visit to India from 22nd to 23rd November," says Nepal's Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai. He adds, "It will be a 34-member government team that will depart from Kathmandu to New Delhi, India. During the visit, the Nepali PM will hold a delegation-level meeting on Monday with his Indian counterpart. Various projects relating to energy will be inaugurated by the two Prime Ministers. Various aspects of cooperation will be signed and exchanged. After the delegation-level talks, the two Prime Ministers will hold a joint press conference. Nepali PM will also call on the President of India, Droupadi Murmu. Nepali PM will also lay a wreath at Mahatma Gandhi's memorial at Rajghat. articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Police said 124 people linked to the Awami League had been arrested in the capital Dhaka over the past 24 hours, without providing further details

Fresh arson attacks erupted in Bangladesh on Friday (November 20, 2026) as authorities restored communications with the hometown of convicted former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, after days of unrest over her planned return from exile.

Ms. Hasina, 79, has vowed to return to Bangladesh in December from India, despite being sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity over a deadly crackdown during the 2024 uprising that ousted her.
Ms. Hasina's former ruling party, the Awami League, whose activities are now banned, called for strikes this week to mark the anniversary of the day Ms. Hasina received her death sentence.
Hundreds of paramilitary troops have been deployed to contain the unrest, in which at least three people have been killed.
A petrol bomb was hurled at the residence of a junior Foreign Minister, Humaiun Kobir, in the northeastern city of Sylhet on Friday (November 20, 2026), police said.
Mr. Kobir said Dhaka would deal with attacks "very firmly".
"It is not possible to bring back a 'fled terrorist' by throwing petrol bombs," he told reporters on Friday (November 20, 2026).
Ms. Hasina has said repeatedly she wants to return next month, telling AFP in an email this week that she was "fully aware" she could be hanged.
Attackers also set fire to the home of a former junior Foreign Minister from the Awami League in Rajshahi on Thursday (November 19, 2026).
Protesters wielding machetes also torched a police station in Gopalganj, Ms. Hasina's political stronghold, the same day. Communications have since been restored.

articles.title: FDA sets up council for post-market review of vaccines, gene therapies
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The FDA said the council is intended to improve accountability and transparency as biologic products grow increasingly complex, particularly in cell and gene therapy, a sector that has seen rapid regulatory expansion in recent years

The US Food and Drug Administration said on Thursday it had established a new internal safety body within its biologics center, formalizing independent oversight of approved products such as vaccines, gene therapies and blood products once they reach the market.

The CBER Safety Council will report directly to the director of the FDA’s Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, structurally separating post-market safety reviews from the offices responsible for approving those products, the agency said.

The council supersedes CBER’s existing Safety Working Group, bringing together senior scientific and regulatory officials to review safety signals, conduct benefit-risk assessments and recommend regulatory actions as warranted.

The new structure formalizes an independent post-market review process at a time when regulators face mounting pressure to closely monitor newer biologic products, including gene and cell therapies, after approval, when they are used across far broader patient populations.
Its mandate will cover emerging safety concerns, potential labeling changes, risk-management measures and safety-related post-market studies, as well as advising on potential market withdrawals.

The FDA said the council is intended to improve accountability and transparency as biologic products grow increasingly complex, particularly in cell and gene therapy, a sector that has seen rapid regulatory expansion in recent years.

The council will coordinate with external bodies including the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the National Institutes of Health, drawing on surveillance systems such as the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) and the FDA Sentinel program.
The council takes effect on November 19; the agency said additional details on its structure and membership will be released later.

The US Food and Drug Administration said on Thursday it had established a new internal safety body within its biologics center, formalizing independent oversight of approved products such as vaccines, gene therapies and blood products once they reach the market.

The CBER Safety Council will report directly to the director of the FDA’s Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, structurally separating post-market safety reviews from the offices responsible for approving those products, the agency said.

The council supersedes CBER’s existing Safety Working Group, bringing together senior scientific and regulatory officials to review safety signals, conduct benefit-risk assessments and recommend regulatory actions as warranted.

The new structure formalizes an independent post-market review process at a time when regulators face mounting pressure to closely monitor newer biologic products, including gene and cell therapies, after approval, when they are used across far broader patient populations.

Its mandate will cover emerging safety concerns, potential labeling changes, risk-management measures and safety-related post-market studies, as well as advising on potential market withdrawals.

The FDA said the council is intended to improve accountability and transparency as biologic products grow increasingly complex, particularly in cell and gene therapy, a sector that has seen rapid regulatory expansion in recent years.

The council will coordinate with external bodies including the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the National Institutes of Health, drawing on surveillance systems such as the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) and the FDA Sentinel program.

The council takes effect on November 19; the agency said additional details on its structure and membership will be released later.

fullParagraphs: Under the 2026 Float and Freeze option, candidates can carry forward their allotments without completing admission formalities, and even if their seats remain unchanged in Round 3, they can choose not to join; this flexibility has had significant implications in seat utilisation

Even as millions of candidates competed for admission, several undergraduate MBBS seats remained vacant during the NEET-UG 2026 counselling. Over 3,000-3,400 vacancies were reported after the initial All India Quota (AIQ) and State rounds, with approximately 410 seats still unfilled in deemed universities even after the Special Stray Vacancy Round.
(Sign up for THEdge , The Hindu’s weekly education newsletter.)

While government medical college seats were all filled, most remaining vacancies were in deemed universities. States such as Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karnataka accounted for a significant share of these vacancies, raising concerns about high fees, seat utilisation and equitable access to medical education.

Of these, 64,121 seats are available in government medical colleges, while the remaining 76,543 seats are in the private medical sector. The latter comprises 14,299 seats in deemed university medical colleges and 62,244 seats in self-financing private medical colleges. Thus, more than 54% of the total MBBS seats in the country are concentrated in the private medical sector, where the cost of medical education is generally substantially higher than in government institutions.

articles.title: Cheetah brought from Botswana gives birth to four cubs at Kuno
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: With these four new arrivals, India’s cheetah population has risen to 62, including 43 Indian-born individuals

A two-and-a-half-year-old cheetah, KOMG 3, brought from Botswana, gave birth to four healthy cubs in the wild at Madhya Pradesh’s Kuno National Park on Friday (November 20, 2026), Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav said.
Calling the development a matter of pride for Madhya Pradesh and the entire country, Chief Minister Mohan Yadav said it was a historic achievement for Project Cheetah.
In a post on X, Bhupender Yadav said KOMG 3 is the first cheetah from Botswana to give birth in India.
“This is a landmark moment for Project Cheetah and a proud milestone in India’s journey towards restoring a viable cheetah population,” he added.
This is the second recorded birth in the wild since the reintroduction programme began in 2022.
With these four new arrivals, India’s cheetah population has risen to 62, including 43 Indian-born individuals.
“Every such birth strengthens our hope, deepens our commitment, and reminds us that conservation is a journey of patience, perseverance and collective effort,” Mr. Yadav said.
He also acknowledged the dedication, commitment and hard work of project managers, veterinarians, frontline forest staff and everyone working tirelessly for the success of Project Cheetah.

In a statement, CM Mohan Yadav said, “This is a matter of pride for Madhya Pradesh and the entire country. The birth of cubs in India for the first time by a female cheetah from Botswana is a historic achievement of Project Cheetah.

“This is an important and encouraging step towards restoring a viable cheetah population in India. KOMG 3, a female cheetah, gave birth to four healthy cubs in natural conditions after spending more than four months in the wild.”

fullParagraphs: India’s cheetah population has risen to 52, including 32 cubs born in the country, as Project Cheetah completes four years on September 17, 2026, with officials highlighting the survival of cubs, breeding success and the expansion of the animals into open forest areas as key milestones.
Cheetah brought from Botswana gives birth to four cubs at Kuno
On September 17, 2022, Prime Minister Narendra Modi released eight wild cheetahs from Namibia into special enclosures at Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh.
The next phase of the cheetah restoration programme involves expanding suitable habitat for cheetahs and establishing a comprehensive, long term cheetah meta population in India.

While 49 cheetahs are in Kuno National Park, three others are in Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary, both in Madhya Pradesh. Over the last four years, many important milestones have been achieved, ranging from the reintroduction of cheetahs to breeding, survival of cubs and expansion into open forest, an official said in a statement.
The journey that began in Namibia on the distant African continent has now reached Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary. A total of 32 cheetahs were born in India, officials said.

The success in cheetah breeding and expansion was achieved by learning from difficulties. “The team faced many challenges in the first year of cheetah reintroduction. During this time, they gained experience in cheetah behaviour, health, and management adapted to Indian conditions,” an official said.
In the next year, the focus shifted to the survival and development of cubs born in India. According to the document, 13 cubs survived for more than a year after birth.

In the third year, 2025, cheetahs were released into open forest areas. They were monitored 24 hours a day across an interstate landscape spanning 12 districts, officials said, adding that the cheetahs gradually adapted to new areas.
The establishment of breeding females and the successful survival of the second generation of cubs in the fourth year are considered significant achievements of the programme, they said.

articles.title: Three to tango: On Trump, Xi, Putin trilateral summit
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: U.S., China, Russia must draw up a roadmap for talks on nuclear weapons

The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

📰 Three to tango: On Trump, Xi, Putin trilateral summit

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions

U.S., China, Russia must draw up a roadmap for talks on nuclear weapons

The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

articles.title: Going public on AI: On Anthropic IPO
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India can no longer afford its silence on the multi-trillion dollar AI arms race

The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Anthropic , PBC is a mile marker in the arms race to develop superintelligent systems driven by generative AI . Traders valued the firm at $1.27 trillion, a denomination that is bound to become more and more familiar in an industry backed by an endless appetite for capital and unprecedented forms of financialisation. Anthropic’s statements emphasise warnings on the safety of its systems and the consequences of unbridled development of advanced systems. In the history of the development of this technology, this PR spin may just be a blip. After all, their testing has led to AI agents that have broken out of sandboxes and infected unsuspecting organisations’ internal systems: a deluge of agentic chaos that is already a reality has led to little signs of the firm backing its words with action. A familiar trend is playing out, with open source LLMs showing frontier capabilities that can back their erratic impulses, appearing in the space of just months, or sometimes weeks. Advocates of pacing the frontier and managing these emerging risks have been marginalised in a way that has little precedent in this century. It is time for governments to get involved, and specifically, for India to raise its voice on these risks, loudly and unequivocally.

While India’s AI industry is nascent, its positions on international forums carry the weight of a sixth of humanity. A mix of cynical calculations and practical considerations have blunted the use of that voice, for example in the U.S.’s hugely destabilising war of choice against Iran, and Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. In taking a strong position on what could be the defining transformation of this decade, India has little to lose, and a lot to contribute. India’s AI policies are geared towards diffusion and research of helpful capabilities that can trickle down to the common citizen. The capabilities that the Union government and State governments seek to boost by leveraging AI are removed from the frontier research wreaking havoc within the information security profession around the world. Out-of-control AI agents promise, moreover, significant disruption to outdated government and private systems online. While India has little commercial leverage to curb San Francisco’s accelerationism, its voice is sure to be noticed. India’s focus on AI in international fora, such as the AI Impact Summit in Delhi, has been on consensus. This approach must change. India cannot be silent amid a U.S.-China technological race which could lead to catastrophic damage. New Delhi must not allow the U.S. to stop it from pushing for AI safety.

articles.title: A step back: On Trump’s no-war, no-deal approach against Iran
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Trump must accept the realities of the war if he wants a deal

Before the November 3 midterm elections, U.S. President Donald Trump had repeatedly threatened to “destroy” Iran unless it entered into a deal with the U.S. to end the war. Since the elections, in which Mr. Trump’s Republican Party suffered a massive defeat , the U.S. President appears to have toned down his rhetoric. Last week, he said he had decided against escalating the military conflict with Iran following requests from America’s Gulf allies. But the U.S. would maintain the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic. Mr. Trump also pulled Vice President J.D. Vance off negotiations with Iran, as the Qatar-mediated talks made no real progress. Iran wants the U.S. to lift the blockade, unfreeze its frozen assets, issue sanctions relief and pull back from the Persian Gulf for direct negotiations on the nuclear programme to restart. The U.S., which calls Iran’s demands “outrageous”, has now adopted a no-war, no-deal approach , hoping that the economic blockade would force Tehran to offer concessions in the near future. Mr. Trump’s retreat from the threats reflects the realities on the ground. Before the U.S. and Israel launched this war by assassinating Iran’s Supreme Leader on February 28, Tehran was ready to make concessions. The U.S. and Israel carried out heavy bombing for 40 days but achieved none of their declared objectives. There is no guarantee that another round of strikes would force Iran to change its position. And the war, as the midterm results show, remains very unpopular in America.

Mr. Trump has only himself, and Benjamin Netanyahu, to blame for the predicament he is in. He is the one who sabotaged a functioning Obama-era nuclear deal in 2018 that had denied Iran a path towards the nuclear bomb. Mr. Trump joined Israel’s unprovoked war on Iran in June 2025 and declared that he had “obliterated” Iran’s nuclear programme. And the same Mr. Trump started the current war, just eight months later, over the same nuclear programme. The Iranian state has survived, though Iranians are facing enormous economic woes. Tehran shut the Strait of Hormuz, pumping up global energy prices. Iran’s counterattacks have either destroyed or damaged America’s bases in the Persian Gulf. High oil prices and inflation turned the American electorate against the Republican party, while in Israel, Mr. Netanyahu, despite war rhetoric and racist attacks on the country’s Arab minorities, lost the governing majority. The setbacks are there for anyone to see. Yet, Mr. Trump does not seem to have grasped the seriousness of the situation. His no-war, no-deal approach r isks a resumption of hostilities as Iran has pledged to break the siege. The U.S. has few clear military options unless it is prepared to launch a ground invasion, which would be disastrous. A more rational way forward is to end the war through diplomacy. But for that, Mr. Trump must first accept the strategic reality that he has lost the war.

Trump must accept the realities of the war if he wants a deal

Before the November 3 midterm elections, U.S. President Donald Trump had repeatedly threatened to “destroy” Iran unless it entered into a deal with the U.S. to end the war. Since the elections, in which Mr. Trump’s Republican Party suffered a massive defeat , the U.S. President appears to have toned down his rhetoric. Last week, he said he had decided against escalating the military conflict with Iran following requests from America’s Gulf allies. But the U.S. would maintain the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic. Mr. Trump also pulled Vice President J.D. Vance off negotiations with Iran, as the Qatar-mediated talks made no real progress. Iran wants the U.S. to lift the blockade, unfreeze its frozen assets, issue sanctions relief and pull back from the Persian Gulf for direct negotiations on the nuclear programme to restart. The U.S., which calls Iran’s demands “outrageous”, has now adopted a no-war, no-deal approach , hoping that the economic blockade would force Tehran to offer concessions in the near future. Mr. Trump’s retreat from the threats reflects the realities on the ground. Before the U.S. and Israel launched this war by assassinating Iran’s Supreme Leader on February 28, Tehran was ready to make concessions. The U.S. and Israel carried out heavy bombing for 40 days but achieved none of their declared objectives. There is no guarantee that another round of strikes would force Iran to change its position. And the war, as the midterm results show, remains very unpopular in America.

Mr. Trump has only himself, and Benjamin Netanyahu, to blame for the predicament he is in. He is the one who sabotaged a functioning Obama-era nuclear deal in 2018 that had denied Iran a path towards the nuclear bomb. Mr. Trump joined Israel’s unprovoked war on Iran in June 2025 and declared that he had “obliterated” Iran’s nuclear programme. And the same Mr. Trump started the current war, just eight months later, over the same nuclear programme. The Iranian state has survived, though Iranians are facing enormous economic woes. Tehran shut the Strait of Hormuz, pumping up global energy prices. Iran’s counterattacks have either destroyed or damaged America’s bases in the Persian Gulf. High oil prices and inflation turned the American electorate against the Republican party, while in Israel, Mr. Netanyahu, despite war rhetoric and racist attacks on the country’s Arab minorities, lost the governing majority. The setbacks are there for anyone to see. Yet, Mr. Trump does not seem to have grasped the seriousness of the situation. His no-war, no-deal approach r isks a resumption of hostilities as Iran has pledged to break the siege. The U.S. has few clear military options unless it is prepared to launch a ground invasion, which would be disastrous. A more rational way forward is to end the war through diplomacy. But for that, Mr. Trump must first accept the strategic reality that he has lost the war.

articles.title: Stoop to conquer: On the Opposition’s seat-sharing ahead of U.P. polls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The Congress should scale down its ambition while seeking an alliance with the SP

As Uttar Pradesh heads to the polls in early 2027, a familiar seat-sharing tussle has emerged within the Opposition. The Samajwadi Party and the Congress share an understanding forged during the Lok Sabha elections that earned them a good share of the State’s seats, but the Congress is now reportedly seeking 181 seats , nearly 45% of the 403 Assembly constituencies. It is the latest instance of the dilemma facing the Congress as it seeks revival in States where it has become a marginal force: how to strike a favourable bargain with stronger partners without weakening the coalition against the Bharatiya Janata Party. With discontent rising against the BJP, which still occupies a hegemonic position in the party system , the Opposition feels a wind behind its sails, and its major parties agree that the only way to take on the BJP is a formidable coalition with a compelling, unified message. But the Congress’s attempt to rebuild itself in the Hindi heartland and in States where it once held sway has strained that unity. In Bihar, the Mahagathbandhan failed to reap the benefits of anti-incumbency against the Janata Dal (United)-BJP alliance, partly because it could not tap the full support of the social forces behind the Rashtriya Janata Dal and the Congress, and partly because the Congress took too long to settle seat-sharing for the campaigns to gel. In Tamil Nadu, the Congress held out for more seats from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and delayed the alliance, while infighting produced a lacklustre campaign that left it with the lowest vote share, in the seats it contested, among the alliance partners.

Uttar Pradesh need not go the same way. The demand for 181 seats is overly ambitious for a party that managed a mere 2.33% of the votes in the 399 seats it contested in 2022, when the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested with a 32% vote share. The Congress has a point that the variables have changed since. In 2024, the SP and the Congress together won 43 of U.P.‘s 80 Lok Sabha seats with a 43.2% vote share, just short of the BJP-led alliance’s 43.7%. The Congress won only six of the 17 seats it contested, but its vote share in those six, 44.2%, was marginally ahead of the SP’s 43.4%. The party could also argue that its national campaigns on youth concerns and the state of India’s electoral democracy give it the heft to seek more. But its lack of an efficient State-wide organisation suggests that 181 is too high. The SP remains the strongest Opposition party , having assiduously built a new social coalition of backward classes, Dalits and minorities to take on the majoritarian BJP through local mobilisations. The 2024 arrangement, in which the Congress contested a fifth of the seats, is a more reasonable guide. A well-targeted 100 or so seats would make for a more coherent campaign and a better showing alongside the SP.

The demand for 181 seats is overly ambitious for a party that managed a mere 2.33% of the votes in the 399 seats it contested in 2022, when the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested with a 32% vote share. The Congress has a point that the variables have changed since. In 2024, the SP and the Congress together won 43 of U.P.‘s 80 Lok Sabha seats with a 43.2% vote share, just short of the BJP-led alliance’s 43.7%. The Congress won only six of the 17 seats it contested, but its vote share in those six, 44.2%, was marginally ahead of the SP’s 43.4%. The party could also argue that its national campaigns on youth concerns and the state of India’s electoral democracy give it the heft to seek more. But its lack of an efficient State-wide organisation suggests that 181 is too high. The SP remains the strongest Opposition party , having assiduously built a new social coalition of backward classes, Dalits and minorities to take on the majoritarian BJP through local mobilisations. The 2024 arrangement, in which the Congress contested a fifth of the seats, is a more reasonable guide. A well-targeted 100 or so seats would make for a more coherent campaign and a better showing alongside the SP.

articles.title: Many imperatives: On India’s Asia diplomacy
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India must shore up its partnerships in the Asian region

Each year, the summits of the 11-member Association of South-East Asian Nations mark an important moment on the diplomatic calendar: India is able to interact with all of its partners in the Indo-Pacific and engage global powers at the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s talks with Indo-Pacific players focused on a future shaped “not by competition, but by cooperation”. This year, the summit in Manila hosted by the Philippines had many other imperatives. These were the first ASEAN summits since the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran and Iran’s Hormuz blockade and strikes on Gulf countries that have upended energy and trade across South and South East Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world during the EAS was aimed as much at leaders from the U.S., Russia and China as it was for the region. The visit had a bilateral context — the Philippines and India have intensified ties considerably in the past year, since the visit of President Bongbong Marcos to Delhi in August 2025, including the upgradation of the Strategic Partnership, maritime exchanges and negotiations over the supply of more Indian-made Brahmos missile battery systems to the Philippines. This year, after months of concerns about U.S. President Donald Trump’s lack of interest in the Quad grouping, the U.S. decided to host a summit of U.S.-India-Australia-Japan Quad leaders on the side-lines of the ASEAN summits, the first time the summit has been held in a non-Quad country.

Given the stakes, there were several outcomes from all the three summits that PM Modi attended back-to-back on Tuesday — the ASEAN India Summit launched a new cooperation on disaster management, and the East Asia Summit focused on countering cyber-crime. PM Modi’s announcement that India would give all ASEAN citizens free tourist visas is expected to increase people-to-people interactions and trade. At the Quad summit, President Trump made a number of announcements including the launch of a Quad Business leaders forum, to be held in Mumbai next year, and the first Quad naval exercises with patrol aircraft. However, the outcomes in Manila paled in significance to the anticipation over Mr. Trump’s next stop in Shenzhen for the Asia Pacific Economic Conference (APEC), with an unprecedented three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping planned on Thursday. New Delhi must watch the outcomes of that summit among the “global superpowers” much more closely.
Editorial Context: Many imperatives: On India’s Asia diplomacy. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.
